## Service history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Service history")]

### With the hunter-killer groups

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: With the hunter-killer groups")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Declaration_of_war_naval_message.jpg/250px-Declaration_of_war_naval_message.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Declaration_of_war_naval_message.jpg)

The message sent to the ship informing her of the commencing of hostilities on 3 September 1939

The outbreak of the Second World War on 1 September 1939 had been presaged by Germany's [U-boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-boat "U-boat") fleet taking up positions off the British coast, where they could intercept British shipping.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Edwards18-28) Within hours of Britain and France declaring war on Germany, the passenger ship [SS _Athenia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Athenia_(1922) "SS Athenia (1922)") was torpedoed by [_U-30_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-30_(1936) "German submarine U-30 (1936)"), the first of over 65,000 tons of shipping sunk by U-boats during the first week of the war.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Edwards18-28)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_74-7-29)_Ark Royal_ was deployed with the Home Fleet in the [North Western Approaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Approaches "Western Approaches") as part of a "hunter-killer" group, consisting of a flotilla of destroyers and other anti-submarine vessels grouped around an aircraft carrier; either [_Courageous_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Courageous_(50) "HMS Courageous (50)"), [_Hermes_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hermes_(95) "HMS Hermes (95)") or _Ark Royal_. Carrier-borne aircraft could increase the area searched for U-boats, but made the carriers tempting targets.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_74-7-29)

On 14 September, _Ark Royal_ received a distress call from [SS _Fanad Head_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Fanad_Head "SS Fanad Head"), which was 200 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (230 mi; 370 km) away under pursuit from the surfaced _U-30_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-fanad-30)_Ark Royal_ launched aircraft to aid the merchant ship, but was spotted by [_U-39_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-39_(1938) "German submarine U-39 (1938)"), which launched two torpedoes.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-fanad-30)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Edwards87-31) Lookouts spotted the torpedo tracks and _Ark Royal_ turned towards the attack, reducing her cross-section and causing the torpedoes to miss and explode harmlessly astern.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_74-7-29) Three [F-class destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_and_F-class_destroyer "E and F-class destroyer") escorting the carrier began to [depth charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge")_U-39_, and forced her to the surface.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Edwards87-31) The German crew abandoned ship before _U-39_ sank—the first U-boat lost during the war.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Edwards87-31)_Ark Royal_'s aircraft reached _Fanad Head_, which was in the hands of a German boarding party.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-fanad-30) The Skuas unsuccessfully attacked _U-30_: two crashed when caught by the blast of their own bombs.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-fanad-30) The U-boat escaped after rescuing the boarding party and the pilots of the downed aircraft (both observers had drowned), and torpedoing the _Fanad Head_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-fanad-30)

_Ark Royal_ returned to base in [Loch Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ewe "Loch Ewe"), where she and her crew were inspected by [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill"). The sinking of _U-39_ was hailed as important to morale. However, the failed attack on _Ark Royal_, and the successful attack on _Courageous_ on 17 September, convinced the Admiralty it was too dangerous to risk aircraft carriers in this way, and carrier-centred hunter-killer groups were abandoned.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_74-7-29)

### Another near miss

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Another near miss")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/HMS_Ark_Royal_h85716.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_h85716.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_h85716.jpg)

HMS _Ark Royal_ in 1939, with Swordfish of [820 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/820_Naval_Air_Squadron "820 Naval Air Squadron") passing overhead

On 25 September 1939, _Ark Royal_ helped rescue the submarine [_Spearfish_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Spearfish "HMS Spearfish"), which had been damaged by German warships off Horn Reefs, in the [Kattegat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattegat "Kattegat").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-32) While returning to port with _Spearfish_ and the battleships [_Nelson_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Nelson_(28) "HMS Nelson (28)") and [_Rodney_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Rodney_(29) "HMS Rodney (29)") on 26 September, the ships were located by three _[Luftwaffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luftwaffe "Luftwaffe")_[Dornier Do 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dornier_Do_18 "Dornier Do 18")[seaplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaplane "Seaplane").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13)_Ark Royal_ launched three Blackburn Skuas to disperse them; one Dornier was shot down in an event propagandised as first British aerial kill of the war (later it was learned that the pilot of a [Fairey Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Battle "Fairey Battle") achieved the first kill).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Westwood-23)

The air commander aboard _Ark Royal_—aware that the surviving Dorniers would report the location of the British ships—ordered the aircraft to be secured and the anti-aircraft weapons readied.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-33) Four [Junkers Ju 88](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junkers_Ju_88 "Junkers Ju 88")[bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomber "Bomber")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-34) of the _Luftwaffe_ bomber wing [KG 30](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KG_30 "KG 30") soon appeared: three were driven away by anti-aircraft fire, but the fourth launched a 2,200-pound (1,000 kg) bomb at the carrier. _Ark Royal_ turned hard to starboard, heeling over and avoiding the bomb, which landed in the ocean 100 feet (30 m) off her starboard bow and sent a spout of water over the ship. The German pilots did not see if the carrier had been hit, and a reconnaissance flight later located the two battleships, but not _Ark Royal_. Based on this information, the Germans incorrectly claimed that _Ark Royal_ had sunk.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross84.5-35) To prove the German propaganda false before it had a negative effect on Britain's allies, Winston Churchill reassured United States President [Franklin Delano Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_Delano_Roosevelt "Franklin Delano Roosevelt") that the carrier was undamaged and invited the US naval attaché to view _Ark Royal_ in dock.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross84.5-35) The British naval attaché in Rome was instructed to assure Italian Prime Minister [Benito Mussolini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini "Benito Mussolini") that the ship was still in service.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross84.5-35) This was an embarrassment for [Goebbels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goebbels "Goebbels") and [Nazi propaganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_propaganda "Nazi propaganda").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-36)

### Hunting the _Graf Spee_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Hunting the Graf Spee")]

In October 1939, _Ark Royal_ was redeployed to [Freetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freetown "Freetown") to operate off the African coast in the hunt for the German [commerce raider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce_raider "Commerce raider")[_Admiral Graf Spee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_cruiser_Admiral_Graf_Spee "German cruiser Admiral Graf Spee"). The carrier was assigned to [Force K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_K "Force K"), and sailed with the battlecruiser [_Renown_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Renown_(1916) "HMS Renown (1916)") to the South Atlantic.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13) On 9 October, aircraft from _Ark Royal_ spotted the German tanker[_Altmark_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_tanker_Altmark "German tanker Altmark"), which supplied _Graf Spee_. The tanker was disguised as the US vessel _Delmar_, which fooled the British into passing her by.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-37) On 5 November, _Ark Royal_ captured the German merchant [SS _Uhenfels_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Uhenfels "SS Uhenfels"), which was attempting to reach Germany. The ship was later taken into British service as a cargo ship[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson53-38) and renamed _Empire Ability_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Mitchell431-39) Several neutral merchant ships were also spotted by the carrier's aircraft, twice causing crews to believe they were under attack and abandon ship.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson42-40) A note explaining the situation was dropped in a bag to a Norwegian vessel's crew, and they re-boarded; an attempt to repeat this exercise with a Belgian crew failed when the bag was dropped down the ship's funnel.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson42-40)

On 14 December 1939, _Graf Spee_ had put into [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo") to repair damage received during the [battle of the River Plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_River_Plate "Battle of the River Plate"). Two Royal Navy cruisers followed the raider, and patrolled the harbour entrance while reporting _Graf Spee_'s position to the fleet. _Ark Royal_ and _Renown_ were dispatched to join the British ships outside the harbour, but as they were 36 hours away, the British naval attaché came up with a plan to make the Germans believe that the two capital ships had already arrived. An order for fuel for _Ark Royal_ was placed at [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), 140 miles (230 km) west of Montevideo. This was leaked to the press, passed on to the German embassy in Montevideo, and given to _Graf Spee_'s captain, [Hans Langsdorff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hans_Langsdorff "Hans Langsdorff").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_94-6-41) This contributed to Langsdorff's decision to scuttle his ship.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_94-6-41)

### Return to the fleet

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Return to the fleet")]

With _Graf Spee_ sunk, _Ark Royal_ remained in the Atlantic for a short time before escorting the damaged [heavy cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_cruiser "Heavy cruiser")[_Exeter_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Exeter_(68) "HMS Exeter (68)") back to [Devonport Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport"), where they arrived in February.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13) Following this, _Ark Royal_ proceeded to [Portsmouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portsmouth "Portsmouth") to take on supplies and personnel, before sailing to [Scapa Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapa_Flow "Scapa Flow"). On arrival, she transferred her Blackburn Skuas to [Naval Air Station _Hatston_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RNAS_Hatston "RNAS Hatston") to strengthen the anchorage's defences.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter3-42)_Ark Royal_ was then assigned to the Mediterranean Fleet for exercises, departing Scapa Flow on 22 March 1940 and heading for [Alexandria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandria "Alexandria") with the aircraft carrier [_Glorious_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Glorious "HMS Glorious").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13) The carriers arrived in the Eastern Mediterranean on 8 April, but the exercises were cancelled a day later. The ships sailed to Gibraltar to await orders.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter3-42)

German forces had invaded Norway as part of [Operation Weserübung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Weser%C3%BCbung "Operation Weserübung") on 9 April, and had secured sections of the coast. Attempts by the Royal Navy to operate in support of British troops failed; air attacks had overwhelmed the ships, sinking [_Gurkha_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Gurkha_(F20) "HMS Gurkha (F20)") and nearly sinking [_Suffolk_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Suffolk_(55) "HMS Suffolk (55)"). Realising that the British ships required air cover, but aware that the Norwegian coast was outside the range of British land-based aircraft, the Admiralty recalled _Ark Royal_ and _Glorious_ from the Mediterranean on 16 April.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter3-42)

### Norwegian campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Norwegian campaign")]

_Ark Royal_ and _Glorious_ arrived at Scapa Flow on 23 April 1940 and were immediately redeployed as part of Operation DX, sailing to Norway with the cruisers [_Curlew_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Curlew_(D42) "HMS Curlew (D42)") and [_Berwick_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Berwick_(65) "HMS Berwick (65)") and screened by the destroyers [_Hyperion_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hyperion_(H97) "HMS Hyperion (H97)"), [_Hereward_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hereward_(H93) "HMS Hereward (H93)"), [_Hasty_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hasty_(H24) "HMS Hasty (H24)"), [_Fearless_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Fearless_(H67) "HMS Fearless (H67)"), [_Fury_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Fury_(H76) "HMS Fury (H76)") and [_Juno_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Juno_(F46) "HMS Juno (F46)"). This was the first time the Royal Navy had deployed carriers with the primary purpose of providing fighter protection for other warships.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13) The ships took up position on 25 April off the coast; _Ark Royal_ positioned 120 nautical miles (220 km; 140 mi) offshore to reduce the chance of air attacks. The carrier's aircraft conducted anti-submarine patrols, provided fighter support for other ships, and carried out strikes against shipping and shore targets.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_112-26)_Ark Royal_ returned to Scapa Flow on 27 April to refuel and replace lost and damaged aircraft, before heading back on the same day with the battleship [_Valiant_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Valiant_(1914) "HMS Valiant (1914)") as escort.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13) During the return, _Ark Royal_ came under air attack from German [Junkers Ju 88](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junkers_Ju_88 "Junkers Ju 88") and [Heinkel He 111](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinkel_He_111 "Heinkel He 111") bombers operating from Norway. The carrier was undamaged, and resumed position on 29 April.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson97-43)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Blackburn_Skua_landing_on_HMS_Ark_Royal.jpg/250px-Blackburn_Skua_landing_on_HMS_Ark_Royal.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Blackburn_Skua_landing_on_HMS_Ark_Royal.jpg)

A [Blackburn Skua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Skua "Blackburn Skua") landing on _Ark Royal_. The Skuas were the mainstay of the Fleet Air Arm during the early Second World War. Also visible are the arrestor wires strung across the flight deck.

By this point, the British high command had realised that they could not hold the Germans in southern Norway. The evacuation of Allied troops from [Molde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molde_(town) "Molde (town)") and [Åndalsnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%85ndalsnes "Åndalsnes") began, with _Ark Royal_ providing air cover from 30 April. On 1 May, the Germans tried to sink the carrier, with numerous air attacks through the day. _Ark Royal_'s fighters and a heavy anti-aircraft barrage drove off the enemy, and although several bombs were dropped at the carrier, none hit.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson97-43) The evacuations of Molde and Andalsnes were completed on 3 May, and the carrier was recalled to Scapa Flow to refuel and rearm. While in port, Captain Arthur Power left the ship for a promotion to the Admiralty, and was replaced by Captain [Cedric Holland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_Holland "Cedric Holland").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-44) On return to Norway, _Ark Royal_ was told to provide air cover for operations around [Narvik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narvik "Narvik"), including the landing of French troops on 13 May.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross119-45) She was joined on 18 May by the carriers _Glorious_ and _Furious_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13)

Despite these efforts, it was clear by the end of May that French forces were on the verge of collapse and Norway was a sideshow compared to the German advance to the English Channel.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross119-45)[Operation Alphabet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Alphabet "Operation Alphabet") was instigated to move Allied troops from Narvik to Britain. _Ark Royal_ and _Glorious_—screened by the destroyers [_Highlander_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Highlander_(H44) "HMS Highlander (H44)"), [_Diana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Diana_(H49) "HMS Diana (H49)"), [_Acasta_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Acasta_(H09) "HMS Acasta (H09)"), [_Ardent_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ardent_(H41) "HMS Ardent (H41)"), and [_Acheron_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Acheron_(H45) "HMS Acheron (H45)")—sailed from Scapa Flow on 1 June to cover the evacuation, which commenced the next day. _Ark Royal_ carried out air patrols and bombing raids from 3–6 June, before redeploying to Narvik on 7 June. The next day, _Glorious_, _Acasta_ and _Ardent_ were sunk by the German battleships [_Scharnhorst_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Scharnhorst "German battleship Scharnhorst") and [_Gneisenau_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Gneisenau "German battleship Gneisenau") while heading back to Britain. _Ark Royal_'s aircraft failed to locate the German ships, which had returned to [Trondheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trondheim "Trondheim").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-46)

The last evacuation convoy left Narvik on 9 June. Before the British ships could withdraw, a raid on Trondheim located _Scharnhorst_. An attack by _Ark Royal_'s Skuas took place at midnight on 13 June.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-47) The attack was a disaster: the escort destroyers [_Antelope_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Antelope_(H36) "HMS Antelope (H36)") and [_Electra_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Electra_(H27) "HMS Electra (H27)") collided while _Ark Royal_ was launching aircraft in fog and returned to England for repairs, eight of the fifteen attacking Skuas were shot down, while _Scharnhorst_ escaped damage.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-48)_Ark Royal_ returned to Scapa Flow the following day, and was reassigned to the Mediterranean Fleet.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-49)

### Mediterranean deployment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mediterranean deployment")]

_Ark Royal_ left Scapa Flow with the battlecruiser [_Hood_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hood "HMS Hood") and three destroyers, arriving at Gibraltar on 23 June 1940. Here she joined [Force H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_H "Force H"), under Sir [James Somerville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fownes_Somerville "James Fownes Somerville"). After the [capitulation of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_France "Battle of France") there was concern that a French fleet at [Mers-el-Kébir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mers-el-K%C3%A9bir "Mers-el-Kébir") might fall under Axis control and tip the balance of power in the Mediterranean.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-50)_Ark Royal_'s captain, Cedric Holland, had been the British naval attaché in Paris, and was sent to negotiate the surrender or scuttling of the French fleet.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-51) Force H was deployed outside the harbour, and when the French admirals refused to agree to the offered terms, opened fire on the French ships. During the [attack on Mers-el-Kébir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Mers-el-K%C3%A9bir "Attack on Mers-el-Kébir"), _Ark Royal_'s aircraft provided targeting information for the British ships.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-52) The French battleship[_Strasbourg_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_battleship_Strasbourg "French battleship Strasbourg") escaped, despite attacks by Swordfish from _Ark Royal_.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-53) Two days after the attack, aircraft from _Ark Royal_ incapacitated the French battleship[_Dunkerque_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_battleship_Dunkerque "French battleship Dunkerque"), which had been beached in the initial attack.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-54)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/HMS_Ark_Royal_planes_landing.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_planes_landing.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_planes_landing.jpg)

A Fairey Swordfish aircraft lands on _Ark Royal_'s flight deck, whilst a Blackburn Skua circles overhead. Photograph taken from [_Kelvin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Kelvin "HMS Kelvin") after the attacks on the Italian Fleet off Sardinia

Having reduced the possibility of a French challenge in the Mediterranean, Force H prepared for attacks on Italian targets, and sailed from Gibraltar on 8 July.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross179-55) The force was attacked by Italian bombers within eight hours of departing, and although Force H escaped damage, Somerville cancelled the raids and ordered the fleet to Gibraltar.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-56) During July, the British colony of Malta came under attack from the Italian air force, with Force H ordered to deliver [Hawker Hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker_Hurricane "Hawker Hurricane") to reinforce the island's air defences. Force H was deployed from 31 July – 4 August, with the carrier [_Argus_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Argus_(I49) "HMS Argus (I49)") used to deliver the aircraft, while _Ark Royal_ provided air cover for the fleet.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross179-55) On 2 August, _Ark Royal_ launched a successful air attack against the Italian air base at [Cagliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagliari "Cagliari").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-57)

Force H remained at Gibraltar until August, when it escorted reinforcements for Admiral [Andrew Cunningham's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cunningham,_1st_Viscount_Cunningham_of_Hyndhope "Andrew Cunningham, 1st Viscount Cunningham of Hyndhope") fleet at Alexandria.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-58) En route, diversionary attacks were planned on Italian air bases at [Elmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elmas "Elmas") and Cagliari to divert attention from both the reinforcement operation and a supply [convoy sailing to Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_Convoy "Malta Convoy"). The successful attacks were carried out on 1 September. Force H then turned back west once the reinforcements had rendezvoused with Cunningham's fleet in the central Mediterranean, without attracting significant attention from the Italian air force.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-59) After returning to Gibraltar, _Ark Royal_ was detached on 6 September and sent to West Africa to support British attempts to encourage [Vichy French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vichy_French "Vichy French") colonies to switch allegiance to the [Free French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_French "Free French"). During negotiations, several Free French aircraft flew from _Ark Royal_, but their aircrews were arrested at [Dakar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakar "Dakar"). Negotiations failed, and bombers from _Ark Royal_ were directed against military installations during the unsuccessful British attempt to take Dakar by force.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-60)_Ark Royal_ then returned to Britain for refit, docking in [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") on 8 October after being escorted by [_Fortune_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Fortune_(H70) "HMS Fortune (H70)"), [_Forester_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Forester_(H74) "HMS Forester (H74)") and [_Greyhound_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Greyhound_(H05) "HMS Greyhound (H05)").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-61) The refit—which lasted until 3 November—included repairs to her machinery and the installation of a new flight deck barrier.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross192-62)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Bombs_falling_astern_of_HMS_Ark_Royal_A2298.jpg/250px-Bombs_falling_astern_of_HMS_Ark_Royal_A2298.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bombs_falling_astern_of_HMS_Ark_Royal_A2298.jpg)

Bombs falling astern of _Ark Royal_ during an attack by Italian aircraft during the [Battle of Cape Spartivento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cape_Spartivento "Battle of Cape Spartivento"). Photograph taken from the cruiser [_Sheffield_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sheffield_(C24) "HMS Sheffield (C24)")

Next, _Ark Royal_—accompanied by [_Barham_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Barham_(04) "HMS Barham (04)"), _Berwick_ and [_Glasgow_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Glasgow_(C21) "HMS Glasgow (C21)")—sailed for Gibraltar, arriving on 6 November.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross192-62) They were deployed with the rest of Force H to escort convoys from Gibraltar to Alexandria and Malta, performing several runs before being assigned to [Operation Collar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Collar_(Convoy) "Operation Collar (Convoy)"), one of 35[convoys to support Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_Convoys "Malta Convoys") between 1940 and 1942, on 25 November. An Italian fleet—led by the battleships [_Giulio Cesare_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_battleship_Giulio_Cesare "Italian battleship Giulio Cesare") and [_Vittorio Veneto_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_battleship_Vittorio_Veneto "Italian battleship Vittorio Veneto")—was dispatched to intercept the convoy.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-63) The Italian fleet was detected by a reconnaissance aircraft from _Ark Royal_ and the carrier launched Swordfish torpedo bombers while the capital ships of Force H turned to meet the enemy.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-64) During the engagement, the [Battle of Cape Spartivento](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Cape_Spartivento "Battle of Cape Spartivento"), the Italian destroyer[_Lanciere_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_destroyer_Lanciere_(1938) "Italian destroyer Lanciere (1938)") was damaged, although it is uncertain if torpedoes from the bombers or British gunfire were responsible. The British mistook _Lanciere_ for a cruiser, while the Italian commanders received incorrect reports that the cruiser [_Bolzano_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_cruiser_Bolzano "Italian cruiser Bolzano") had been hit.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson239-65) British attacks failed to damage any other Italian ships or sink the disabled destroyer, and a retaliatory attack by the Italian air force saw _Ark Royal_ as the subject of multiple bombing runs, none of which hit.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson239-65) The battle had no clear result, although the British convoy reached its destination unscathed.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-66)

On 14 December 1940, _Ark Royal_ and Force H were redeployed from Gibraltar to the Atlantic to search the [Azores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azores "Azores") for commerce raiders. _Ark Royal_ returned to the Mediterranean on 20 December, and escorted the battleship [_Malaya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Malaya "HMS Malaya") and merchant ships from Malta until 27 December.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-67) Force H then became involved in [Operation Excess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Excess "Operation Excess"), a plan to move convoys through the Mediterranean to support the [Western Desert Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Desert_Force "Western Desert Force"), which was trying to push Italian land forces from Egypt into Libya. Over the next month, British control of the Mediterranean theatre was weakened, particularly by the entry of the _Luftwaffe_ and the near-loss of the aircraft carrier [_Illustrious_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Illustrious_(87) "HMS Illustrious (87)").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-68) The Mediterranean Fleet was under pressure from Axis forces in the Eastern Mediterranean, while the British port at Gibraltar was likely to be lost if the Spanish chose to ally with the Germans instead of remaining [neutral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-belligerent "Non-belligerent"). To relieve the Mediterranean Fleet, while demonstrating British strength to the Spanish, the Admiralty and Admiral Cunningham planned to use _Ark Royal_'s Swordfish bombers in raids against Italian targets, supported by bombardment from heavy fleet units. The first bombing, on 2 January against the Tirso Dam in [Sardinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardinia "Sardinia"), was unsuccessful but _Ark Royal_'s Swordfish bombers were more successful on 6 January, when they bombed the port city of [Genoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genoa "Genoa").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-69) The carrier's aircraft also covered the battlecruiser _Renown_ and battleship _Malaya_ while they shelled the port in [Operation Grog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Grog "Operation Grog"). On 9 January, _Ark Royal_ launched aircraft to bomb an oil refinery at [La Spezia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Spezia "La Spezia"), and to lay mines in the harbour. Both operations were successful.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-70)

### Searching for _Scharnhorst_ and _Gneisenau_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Searching for Scharnhorst and Gneisenau")]

In early February 1941, the battleships _Scharnhorst_ and _Gneisenau_ headed into the Atlantic during [Operation Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Berlin_(Atlantic) "Operation Berlin (Atlantic)") on the orders of Grand Admiral [Erich Raeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_Raeder "Erich Raeder"), commander of the German Navy. They were to disrupt Allied shipping and draw capital ships from other areas. On 8 March, Force H and _Ark Royal_ were ordered to the [Canary Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canary_Islands "Canary Islands") to search for the battleships, and to cover convoys crossing from the United States.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-71)_Ark Royal_ used her aircraft to search for captured ships returning to Germany under the control of [prize crews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prize_crew "Prize crew"). Three ships were located on 19 March: two scuttled themselves, while the third—SS _Polykarp_— reached France.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-72)

On the evening of 21 March 1941 a Fairey Fulmar from _Ark Royal_ stumbled across _Scharnhorst_ and _Gneisenau_ at sea. Because of a radio malfunction, the crew had to return to _Ark Royal_ to report, by which time the German ships had escaped under fog.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-73) The next day, _Ark Royal_ re-established air patrols in the hope of re-locating the raiders. During the day, a catapult malfunction destroyed a Fairey Swordfish; flinging the fuselage into the sea ahead of the carrier. Unable to stop, _Ark Royal_ ran over the Swordfish and was overhead when the aircraft's depth charges detonated.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-74)_Scharnhorst_ and _Gneisenau_ reached [Brest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brest,_France "Brest, France") without British harassment, while _Ark Royal_ returned to Gibraltar for repairs, arriving on 24 March.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-75)

### Malta convoys and Operation Tiger

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Malta convoys and Operation Tiger")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/H.M.S._Renown_and_Ark_Royal.jpg/250px-H.M.S._Renown_and_Ark_Royal.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:H.M.S._Renown_and_Ark_Royal.jpg)

_Ark Royal_ at sea with the battlecruiser _Renown_

_Ark Royal_ spent April alternating between covering convoys and delivering aircraft to Malta and forays into the Atlantic to hunt commerce raiders. By May 1941, [Erwin Rommel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erwin_Rommel "Erwin Rommel")'s _[Afrika Korps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrika\_Korps "Afrika Korps")_ were driving through North Africa towards the [Suez Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Canal "Suez Canal"), pushing the Western Desert Force before them. With British forces close to collapse and strategic locations threatened, the British High Command risked sending a reinforcement convoy across the Mediterranean to Alexandria. The convoy consisted of five large transport ships, escorted by _Ark Royal_, the battlecruiser _Renown_, the battleship [_Queen Elizabeth_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Queen_Elizabeth_(1913) "HMS Queen Elizabeth (1913)"), the cruisers [_Sheffield_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sheffield_(C24) "HMS Sheffield (C24)"), [_Naiad_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Naiad_(93) "HMS Naiad (93)"), [_Fiji_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Fiji "HMS Fiji"), and [_Gloucester_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Gloucester_(62) "HMS Gloucester (62)"), and screened by destroyers of the 5th Destroyer Flotilla.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-76) Prior to _Ark Royal_'s departure, Captain Holland left to recuperate from stress and poor health, and was replaced by Captain [Loben Maund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loben_Edward_Harold_Maund "Loben Edward Harold Maund").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-77) The convoy left Gibraltar on 6 May, and was detected by Italian aircraft. The convoy—limited to 14 knots (26 km/h; 16 mph) and escorted by so many capital ships—was such a tempting target that Italian and German aircraft were mobilised.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-78)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/HMS_ARK_ROYAL_and_HMS_RENOWN_firing_at_Italian_torpedo_bombers_during_an_attack_on_a_British_convoy_off_Sicily%2C_April_1941._A4017.jpg/250px-HMS_ARK_ROYAL_and_HMS_RENOWN_firing_at_Italian_torpedo_bombers_during_an_attack_on_a_British_convoy_off_Sicily%2C_April_1941._A4017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_ARK_ROYAL_and_HMS_RENOWN_firing_at_Italian_torpedo_bombers_during_an_attack_on_a_British_convoy_off_Sicily,_April_1941._A4017.jpg)

An intense anti-aircraft barrage is visible during an attack by Italian torpedo bombers on Force H. _Ark Royal_ is on the left, with an Italian aircraft over her bows, and HMS _Renown_ to the right.

The British convoy came under air attack on 8 May, first by the Italian air force, then the German _Luftwaffe_. Over the day, 12 of _Ark Royal_'s Fairey Fulmars (the maximum number available) drove off over 50 aircraft, with the assistance of targeting information from _Sheffield_'s radar and anti-aircraft fire from the escorts.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-79)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-80) During the initial waves, one Fulmar was lost, killing Flight Lieutenant Rupert Tillard and Lieutenant Mark Somerville; another was destroyed with the aircrew recovered, while several others were damaged.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Ross249-81) Consequently, only seven were able to face the main _Luftwaffe_ force of 34 aircraft, while an attack just before dark was driven off by two aircraft and heavy fire from the ships.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Ross249-81) The convoy survived without serious damage: the only casualties were to mines, with the _Empire Song_ sunk and _New Zealand Star_ damaged but able to reach port.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-82)_Ark Royal_ underwent another aerial attack on 12 May, during her return to Gibraltar. Later that month, she and fellow aircraft carrier _Furious_ delivered Hawker Hurricanes to support Malta.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-83)

### Hunting the _Bismarck_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Hunting the Bismarck")]

See also: [Last battle of Bismarck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_battle_of_Bismarck "Last battle of Bismarck")

On 18 May 1941, the German battleship [_Bismarck_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Bismarck "German battleship Bismarck") and heavy cruiser [_Prinz Eugen_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_cruiser_Prinz_Eugen "German cruiser Prinz Eugen") began [Operation Rheinübung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Rhein%C3%BCbung "Operation Rheinübung") by breaking into the Atlantic to raid shipping. After sinking the battlecruiser _Hood_ and damaging the battleship [_Prince of Wales_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Prince_of_Wales_(53) "HMS Prince of Wales (53)") during the [Battle of the Denmark Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Denmark_Strait "Battle of the Denmark Strait"), _Bismarck_ shook off her pursuers and headed for the French Atlantic coast.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-84)_Ark Royal_, _Renown_, and _Sheffield_—accompanied by destroyers [_Faulknor_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Faulknor_(H62) "HMS Faulknor (H62)"), _Foresight_, _Forester_, _Fortune_, [_Foxhound_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Foxhound_(H69) "HMS Foxhound (H69)"), and _Fury_—were dispatched to the Atlantic on 23 May to search for the battleship.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-85) On 26 May, a Swordfish from _Ark Royal_ located _Bismarck_ and began to shadow her, while the Home Fleet was mobilised to pursue.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-86)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/HMS_Ark_Royal_Swordfish.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_Swordfish.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_Swordfish.jpg)

One of _Ark Royal_'s [Fairey Swordfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Swordfish "Fairey Swordfish") returns at low level over the sea after making a torpedo attack on _Bismarck_

At the time of detection, the British ships were 130 nmi (240 km; 150 mi) away and would not catch _Bismarck_ before she reached [Saint-Nazaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Nazaire "Saint-Nazaire"), putting her safely under the air cover of the _Luftwaffe_ once in range and while being repaired at the Normandie drydock. Fifteen Swordfish bombers were armed with torpedoes and sent to delay the ship. _Sheffield_, also shadowing _Bismarck_, was between _Ark Royal_ and _Bismarck_. The aircraft mistook the British cruiser for their target and fired torpedoes. The torpedoes were fitted with unreliable magnetic detonators, which caused most to explode on contact with the water, while _Sheffield_ evaded the rest.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-87) After realising his mistake, one of the pilots signalled 'Sorry for the kipper' to _Sheffield_.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-88)

On return to the carrier, the Swordfish were re-armed with contact-detonator warhead torpedoes, and launched at 19:15 for a second attack; locating and attacking _Bismarck_ just before sunset. Three torpedoes hit the battleship: two detonated forward of the engine rooms, while the third struck the starboard steering compartment and jammed her rudder in a 15° port turn.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-89)_Bismarck_ was forced to sail in circles until a combination of alternating propeller speeds was found which would keep her on a reasonably steady course which, in the prevailing [force 8 wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaufort_scale "Beaufort scale") and [sea state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_state "Sea state"), forced her to sail towards the British warships with almost no manoeuvring capability.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-90) The German battleship was harassed by British destroyers during the night of 26–27 May and suffered heavy attack the next morning, finally sinking at 10:39 hours on 27 May.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-91)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-92)

### Escorting the Malta convoys

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Escorting the Malta convoys")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/ce/HMS_Ark_Royal_planes.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_planes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_planes.jpg)

Six [Blackburn Skuas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Skua "Blackburn Skua") of [No. 800 Squadron Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/800_Naval_Air_Squadron "800 Naval Air Squadron") lined up on deck before taking off

_Ark Royal_ and the ships of Force H returned to Gibraltar on 29 May 1941. Despite the boost in Allied morale from the sinking of the battleship _Bismarck_, the [war in the Mediterranean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_theatre_of_World_War_II "Mediterranean theatre of World War II") was going against the Allies. [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") and [Crete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crete "Crete") had fallen to the Axis Powers, and the _Afrika Korps_ was preparing to launch a final push into [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"). Malta remained an important stronghold in the Mediterranean, but was coming under increased pressure from Italian and German air attacks, and could no longer be supplied from the east since the [Battle of Crete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Crete "Battle of Crete").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-93)

_Ark Royal_ was pressed into service, delivering aircraft to Malta during several supply runs throughout June and July, and escorting the convoys of [Operation Substance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Substance "Operation Substance") in July and [Operation Halberd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Halberd "Operation Halberd") in September. Despite some losses, the convoys succeeded in keeping Malta supplied and fighting.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-94) The continued Allied presence in Malta was a considerable problem for Rommel in Africa, who was losing as much as ⅓ of his supplies from Italy to submarines and bombers based there.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter327-95)[Adolf Hitler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Hitler "Adolf Hitler") decided to send a flotilla of U-boats into the Mediterranean to attack Allied shipping, against the advice of _Großadmiral_ Raeder.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter327-95)

## Final voyage and sinking

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Final voyage and sinking")]

On 10 November 1941, _Ark Royal_ ferried more aircraft to Malta before returning to Gibraltar. Admiral Somerville had been warned of U-boats off the Spanish coast, and reminded Force H to be vigilant.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-96) Also at sea was [Friedrich Guggenberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friedrich_Guggenberger "Friedrich Guggenberger")'s [_U-81_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-81_(1941) "German submarine U-81 (1941)"), which had received a report that Force H was returning to Gibraltar.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter327-95)

On 13 November, at 15:40, the sonar operator aboard the destroyer [_Legion_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Legion_(G74) "HMS Legion (G74)") detected an unidentified sound, but assumed it was the propellers of a nearby destroyer. One minute later, _Ark Royal_ was struck amidships by a torpedo,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-97) between the fuel bunkers and bomb store, and directly below the bridge island.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross332-98) The explosion caused _Ark Royal_ to shake, hurled loaded torpedo-bombers into the air, and killed 44 year old Able Seaman Edward Mitchell, the only man to die in the sinking.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross332-98) The torpedo punched a 130 ft ×30 ft (40 m ×9 m) hole in the ship's bottom and starboard side below the water-line after running deep and hitting the bilge keel, inboard of the side protection system.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Friedman_126-99) The hit caused flooding of the starboard boiler room, main [switchboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_switchboard "Telephone switchboard"), oil tanks, and over 106 feet (32 m) of the ship's starboard bilge. The explosion knocked out all internal communications and the starboard power train, causing the rear half of the ship to lose power.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-100)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking.jpg)

[_Legion_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Legion_(G74) "HMS Legion (G74)") moving alongside the damaged and listing _Ark Royal_ to take off survivors

Immediately after the torpedo strike, Captain Maund ordered the engines to full stop, but with the communications knocked out had to send a runner to the engine room.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson338-101) The ship's continued motion enlarged the hole in the hull, and by the time _Ark Royal_ stopped she had taken on a great deal of water and begun to [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_(watercraft) "List (watercraft)") to starboard, reaching 18° from centre within 20 minutes.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson338-101) Considering the list of _Ark Royal_, and the fact that other carriers, including _Courageous_ and _Glorious_, had sunk rapidly with heavy loss of life, Maund gave the order to abandon ship. The crew were assembled on the flight deck to determine who would remain on board to try to save the ship while _Legion_ came alongside to take off the rest. As a result, comprehensive [damage control measures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damage_control_(maritime) "Damage control (maritime)") were not initiated until 49 minutes after the attack. The flooding spread unchecked, exacerbated by covers and hatches left open during evacuation of the lower decks.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-102)

Water spread to the centreline boiler room, which started to flood from below, and power was lost shipwide when the boiler uptakes became choked; _Ark Royal_ had no backup diesel generators.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-103) About half an hour after the explosion, the carrier appeared to stabilise. Admiral Somerville, determined to save _Ark Royal_, ordered damage control parties back to the carrier before taking the battleship _Malaya_ to Gibraltar to organise salvage efforts. The damage control parties re-lit a boiler, restoring power to the bilge pumps. The destroyer [_Laforey_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Laforey_(G99) "HMS Laforey (G99)") came alongside to provide power and additional pumps, while Swordfish aircraft from Gibraltar flew overhead to supplement anti-submarine patrols.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-104) The tug [_Thames_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMT_Thames "HMT Thames") arrived from Gibraltar at 20:00 and attached a tow line to _Ark Royal_, but the flooding had caused the ship to list more severely. Rising water reached the boiler room fan flat, an uninterrupted compartment running the width of the ship. This forced the shutdown of the restored boiler.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-105)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking_2.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_sinking_2.jpg)

Another photograph showing the degree of the list

The list reached 20° between 02:05 and 02:30, and when 'abandon ship' was declared again at 04:00, had reached 27°.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-106)_Ark Royal_'s complement had been evacuated to _Legion_ by 04:30; with the exception of Mitchell, there were no fatalities. The 1,487 officers and crew were transported to Gibraltar.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-107) The list reached 45° before _Ark Royal_ capsized and sank at 06:19 on 14 November.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-108) Witnesses reported the carrier rolling to 90°, where she remained for three minutes before inverting. _Ark Royal_ then broke in two, the aft sinking within a couple of minutes, followed by the bow.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-109) This was the final, or only ship sinking that [Unsinkable Sam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unsinkable_Sam "Unsinkable Sam") survived.

### Investigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Investigation")]

A [Board of Inquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Board_of_Inquiry "Board of Inquiry") was established to investigate the loss. Based on its findings, Captain [Loben Maund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loben_Maund "Loben Maund") was [court-martialled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court-martial "Court-martial") in February 1942. He was found guilty on two counts of negligence: one of failing to ensure that properly constituted damage control parties had remained on board after the general evacuation, and one of failing to ensure the ship was in a sufficient state of readiness to deal with possible damage.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross372.3-110) The board tempered their judgement with an acknowledgement that a high standard was being expected of Maund, and that he was primarily concerned with the welfare of his crew.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-ross372.3-110)

The Bucknill Committee, which had been set up to investigate the loss of major warships, also produced a report. This report said that the lack of backup power sources was a major design failure, which contributed to the loss: _Ark Royal_ depended on electricity for much of her operation, and once the boilers and steam-driven dynamos were knocked out, the loss of power made damage control difficult. The committee recommended the design of the bulkheads and boiler intakes be improved to decrease the risk of widespread flooding in boiler rooms and machine spaces, while the uninterrupted boiler room flat was criticised. The design flaws were rectified in the [_Illustrious_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illustrious-class_aircraft_carrier "Illustrious-class aircraft carrier")- and [_Implacable_-class aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implacable-class_aircraft_carrier "Implacable-class aircraft carrier"), under construction at the time.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-111)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-112)

The Board of Inquiry closed its report with the observation that _Ark Royal_ had sunk 22 nautical miles (25 mi; 41 km) east of [Europa Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europa_Point "Europa Point"), the southernmost tip of Gibraltar. This was accepted as the wreck location for sixty years.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-113)

## Rediscovery

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Rediscovery")]

The location of the wreck was undetermined until mid-December 2002, when the wreck was discovered by an underwater survey company, C & C Technologies, Inc, using a sonar-equipped autonomous underwater vehicle, 30 nautical miles (35 mi; 56 km) from Gibraltar, at about 3,300 feet (1,000 m) depth.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-hydro2004-114)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-filmcrew-115) The company had been contracted by the BBC as part of a documentary on [maritime archaeology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_archaeology "Maritime archaeology") related to major battles of the Royal Navy.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-filmcrew-115) The _Ark Royal_ wreck lies in two main pieces with the stern section sitting upright and the bow section upside down. 66 feet (20 m) of the bow is separated from the rest of the ship's hull. A large debris field, which includes the funnel and bridge island, parts of the ship that came loose as the carrier sank, and aircraft from the hangars, lies between the two hull sections. Analysis revealed that the port side of the ship hit the seabed first.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-116)

The wreck was found further east than expected. Researchers originally thought the wreck had been carried by [currents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_current "Ocean current") farther into the Mediterranean as she sank—that the ship had travelled eastwards underwater before reaching the seabed.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-117) The presence near the hull pieces of other debris, including a Swordfish bomber that was tipped off the flight deck before the ship rolled, proved this false. If the current had pushed the hull pieces any significant distance sideways as they sank, debris would have been spread over a much wider area. It seems though that eastward currents had affected her progress towards Gibraltar during the time she was under tow.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter377-118)

Study of the wreck also showed that restarting the engines to provide power increased the stresses placed on the hull, adding to the flooding. Once power was then lost, it was impossible to prevent the ship from sinking—her fate was more the result of design flaws than of the actions of her captain.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter377-118)

2.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_ref-6)Norman Friedman: When the flight deck becomes the strength deck, the aircraft hangars are then enclosed within the hull structure. The terms, 'enclosed' and 'open' hangars do not, strictly speaking, refer to a hangar that is closed or open on the sides, but rather to whether the hangar is, respectively, below or above the strength deck
3.   [↑](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_ref-7)Friedman: The flight deck was designed with .75 in of Ducol steel. The enclosed hangar design required a deck of approximately this thickness to ensure adequate hull integrity, so the limited armour protection was a by-product of the enclosed hangar design. The strength deck is designed to carry structural loading in combination with the hull girder and side and bottom plating. Ship's structure above the strength deck is termed 'superstructure'. Ducol steel was an advanced type of high tensile steel which had great strength and was often used to provide armour for splinter protection.

**HMS _Ark Royal_** ([pennant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennant_number "Pennant number") 91) was an [aircraft carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier") of the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") that operated during the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War").

Designed in 1934 to fit the restrictions of the [Washington Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Naval_Treaty "Washington Naval Treaty"), _Ark Royal_ was built by [Cammell Laird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cammell_Laird "Cammell Laird") at [Birkenhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birkenhead "Birkenhead"), England, and completed in November 1938. Her design differed from previous aircraft carriers. _Ark Royal_ was the first ship on which the hangars and [flight deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_deck "Flight deck") were an integral part of the hull, instead of an add-on or part of the [superstructure](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/superstructure "wikt:superstructure"). Designed to carry a large number of aircraft, she had two hangar deck levels. She was used during a period that first saw the extensive use of naval air power; several carrier tactics were developed and refined aboard _Ark Royal_.

_Ark Royal_ operated in some of the most active naval theatres of the Second World War. She was involved in the first aerial [_U_-boat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U-boat "U-boat") kills of the war, [operations off Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_campaign_in_Norway "Allied campaign in Norway"), the [search for the German battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_battle_of_the_battleship_Bismarck "Last battle of the battleship Bismarck")[_Bismarck_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Bismarck "German battleship Bismarck"), and the [Malta Convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta_Convoys "Malta Convoys"). _Ark Royal_ survived several near misses and gained a reputation as a 'lucky ship'. She was torpedoed on 13 November 1941 by the [German submarine _U-81_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-81_(1941) "German submarine U-81 (1941)") and sank the following day. One of her 1,488 crew members was killed. Her sinking was the subject of several inquiries, with investigators keen to know how the carrier was lost in spite of efforts to save the ship and tow her to the naval base at [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar"). They found that several design flaws contributed to the loss, which were rectified in subsequent British carriers.

The wreck was discovered in December 2002 by an American underwater survey company using [sonar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonar "Sonar") mounted on an [autonomous underwater vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_underwater_vehicle "Autonomous underwater vehicle"), under contract from the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") for the filming of a documentary about the ship, at a depth of about 3,300 feet (1,000 m) and about 30 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (56 km; 35 mi) from Gibraltar.

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

In 1923, the [Admiralty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Admiralty "British Admiralty") prepared a 10-year building programme which included an aircraft carrier and 300 aircraft for the [Fleet Air Arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Air_Arm "Fleet Air Arm").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter-3) The economic downturn following the First World War caused it to be postponed. In 1930, the [Director of Naval Construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_Naval_Construction "Director of Naval Construction"), [Sir Arthur Johns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Johns_(naval_architect) "Arthur Johns (naval architect)"), began to update the plans for the carrier by incorporating recently developed technology.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter-3) His aim was to increase the number of aircraft carried by shortening the landing and take-off distances of aircraft using [arrestor gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arresting_gear "Arresting gear") and [compressed steam catapults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_catapult "Aircraft catapult") respectively, which would make more deck space available for storage and aircraft preparation.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter-3)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4) Along with the inclusion of two hangar decks, this allowed _Ark Royal_ to carry up to 72 aircraft, although the development of larger and heavier aircraft during the carrier's construction meant that the actual number carried was between 50 and 60.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-5)_Ark Royal_ featured an enclosed hangar design[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-6) where the flight deck was the 'strength deck'[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-7) and was strongly built with 0.75in (19mm) thick [Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ducol "Ducol") steel plating. The two hangar decks were thus enclosed within the hull girder, which also gave splinter protection to the hangars. The machinery spaces were protected by 4.5-inch (11.4 cm)[belt armour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belt_armour "Belt armour").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4) Three lifts moved aircraft between the hangars and the flight deck.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/HMS_Ark_Royal_19sb2j1.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_19sb2j1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_19sb2j1.jpg)

_Ark Royal_'s flight deck overhung the stern. Her unusual height above the waterline is visible in comparison with the tugboat.

Another feature was the length and height of the flight deck. At 800 feet (240 m), the flight deck was 118 feet (36 m) longer than the keel; the latter dictated by the length of Royal Navy drydocks in [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar") and [Malta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malta "Malta").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4) Due to the twin hangar decks, the flight deck rose to 66 feet (20 m) above the waterline.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson-8)

The [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Naval_Treaty "Washington Naval Treaty") and [London Naval treaties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Naval_Treaty "London Naval Treaty") had restricted warship displacement for a number of nations after the end of the Great War and were both to expire by the end of 1936.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-a-9) With a potential naval arms race developing between Britain, Japan and Italy, the [British government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Her_Majesty's_Government "Her Majesty's Government") sought a [second treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_London_Naval_Treaty "Second London Naval Treaty"), which included limiting the maximum displacement of an aircraft carrier to 23,000 [long tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton "Long ton") (23,000[t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne")). _Ark Royal_ would have to fit this anticipated limit; to conserve weight, armour plating was limited to the belt, engine rooms, and [magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine_(artillery) "Magazine (artillery)"), while [welding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welding "Welding") instead of [rivetting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivet "Rivet") 65% of the hull saved 500 long tons (510 t).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_48-9-10) Installation of an [armoured flight deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armoured_flight_deck "Armoured flight deck") was not possible, as the weight would have placed _Ark Royal_ above the proposed limit, while reducing her endurance and stability.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_48-9-10) The ship was designed with a three-layer [side protection system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side_protection_system "Side protection system") based upon a void-liquid-void scheme very similar to that used on the [_King George V_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_George_V-class_battleship_(1939)#Underwater_protection "King George V-class battleship (1939)") battleships, and was designed to protect against torpedoes with up to a 750-pound (340 kg) warhead.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Friedman_121-12)

The ship was fitted with six boilers, which powered three Parsons geared turbines. The turbines were connected via three driveshafts to three propellers 16 feet (4.9 m) in diameter, to produce a maximum theoretical speed of 30 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (56 km/h; 35 mph).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-14) Speed was important, as with catapults and arrestor gear, _Ark Royal_ would have to turn into the wind to launch and recover aircraft. To avoid endangering other ships with the frequent course changes associated with flight operations, _Ark Royal_ would have to break away from accompanying ships, and catch up on completion. Additionally, as the carrier was not armed for ship-to-ship combat, speed was her main protection against enemy warships.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter-3)

## Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

The deteriorating international situation by 1933, typified by Germany's rearmament and the expansion of Japan and Italy, convinced the British to announce funds for the carrier's construction in the 1934 budget proposals.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-15) The plans were finished by November 1934 and were tendered in February 1935 to [Cammell Laird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cammell_Laird "Cammell Laird") and Company, Ltd, which calculated the cost of the hull at [£](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_pound "British pound")1,496,250 (equivalent to £119 million in 2024)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-inflation-UKGDP-16) and the main machinery at about £500,000 (equivalent to £40 million in 2024).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-navalhistory.net-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-17) The overall cost was estimated to be over £3 million (equivalent to £240 million in 2024), making _Ark Royal_ the most expensive non-battleship ordered by the Royal Navy.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-18) Construction began on Job No.1012 when _Ark Royal_'s keel was laid down on 16 September 1935.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Colledge-19)

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/10/HMS_Ark_Royal_%2891%29_just_after_launching.jpg/250px-HMS_Ark_Royal_%2891%29_just_after_launching.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)_just_after_launching.jpg)

_Ark Royal_ immediately after launching. The lifts on the flight deck and the anti-aircraft positions on the hull are visible.

_Ark Royal_ spent nearly two years in the builder's yard before being launched on 13 April 1937 by [Lady Maud Hoare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maud_Hoare,_Viscountess_Templewood "Maud Hoare, Viscountess Templewood"), wife of [Sir Samuel Hoare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Hoare,_1st_Viscount_Templewood "Samuel Hoare, 1st Viscount Templewood"), then [First Lord of the Admiralty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Commissioner_of_the_Admiralty "Lord Commissioner of the Admiralty"). The bottle of champagne thrown against _Ark Royal_'s bows did not smash until the fourth attempt.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-20) The carrier spent a year [fitting out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitting_out "Fitting out"), was handed over to her first commander, [Captain Arthur Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_John_Power "Arthur John Power"), on 16 November 1938, and was commissioned on 16 December.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Colledge-19) Although intended for the Far East, events in Europe during the carrier's construction, including the [Italian invasion of Abyssinia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italo-Abyssinian_War "Second Italo-Abyssinian War") in 1935 and the [Spanish Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War "Spanish Civil War") in 1936, caused the Admiralty to mark her for deployment with the [Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Fleet "Home Fleet") and [Mediterranean Fleets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_Fleet_(United_Kingdom) "Mediterranean Fleet (United Kingdom)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-21) After her crew joined at the end of 1938, _Ark Royal_ underwent [sea trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_trial "Sea trial") to prepare for service, during which the carrier proved capable of sailing above her theoretical speed, reaching over 31 knots (57.4 km/h; 35.6 mph)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Jameson-8) and in trials during May 1938 _Ark Royal_ achieved 31.2 knots (57.8 km/h; 35.9 mph) with 103,012 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (76,816 kW) at a deep displacement of 27,525 long tons (27,967 t).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-22)

## Armament and aircraft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Armament and aircraft")]

_Ark Royal_'s armament was designed with [anti-aircraft warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") in mind, as aircraft were expected to be the main threat; ships and submarines could be outrun or dealt with by escorts.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Westwood-23)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-24) Her main armament was sixteen [quick-firing 4.5-inch (113 mm)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4.5_inch_naval_gun "QF 4.5 inch naval gun")[dual purpose guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_purpose_gun "Dual purpose gun") in eight twin turrets, four on each side of the hull, controlled by four [Directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_Director "Gun Director") using the [High Angle Control System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Angle_Control_System "High Angle Control System").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4) The original design placed the turrets low on the hull, but was later altered to locate them just below the flight deck, which increased each turret's [field of fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_of_fire_(weaponry) "Field of fire (weaponry)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-BisChant-4) Six[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-pompom-1) 8-barrelled 40-millimetre (1.57 in)[QF 2-pounder "pom-pom" gun mounts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_2-pounder_naval_gun "QF 2-pounder naval gun") were located on the flight deck, in front of and behind the superstructure island, while eight 4-barrelled [.50-inch (12.7 mm) Vickers machine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_.50_machine_gun "Vickers .50 machine gun") were installed on small projecting platforms to the front and rear of the flight deck.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-25)

Sixteen Fleet Air Arm squadrons were posted aboard _Ark Royal_ during her career; an average of five squadrons at any time. On entering service, most of _Ark Royal_'s squadrons were equipped with either [Blackburn Skuas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Skua "Blackburn Skua")—used as fighters and dive bombers—or [Fairey Swordfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Swordfish "Fairey Swordfish"), for reconnaissance and torpedo bombing. From April 1940, squadrons equipped with Skuas were upgraded to [Fairey Fulmars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Fulmar "Fairey Fulmar"); like their predecessors, these were used as fighters and bombers. On occasion, the carrier operated [Blackburn Roc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackburn_Roc "Blackburn Roc") fighter-bombers (from April 1939 – October 1940) and [Fairey Albacore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairey_Albacore "Fairey Albacore") torpedo bombers (during October 1941); these were replacement aircraft used to boost squadron numbers.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-Rossiter_112-26) In June 1940, _Ark Royal_ was host to [701 Naval Air Squadron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/701_Naval_Air_Squadron "701 Naval Air Squadron"), a training squadron which operated [Supermarine Walrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermarine_Walrus "Supermarine Walrus") reconnaissance [amphibians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibious_aircraft "Amphibious aircraft").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Ark_Royal_(91)#cite_note-27)
