_**Musashi**_ ([Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language"): 武蔵; named after [the former Japanese province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musashi_Province "Musashi Province")[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-2)) was one of the [_Yamato_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamato-class_battleship "Yamato-class battleship")[battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battleship "Battleship")[[N 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-4) built for the [Imperial Japanese Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy "Imperial Japanese Navy") (IJN), beginning in the late 1930s. The _Yamato_-class ships were the heaviest and most powerfully armed battleships ever constructed,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-j9-5) displacing almost 72,000 long tons (73,000 t) fully loaded and armed with nine 460-millimetre (18.1 in) main guns. Their [secondary armament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_armament "Secondary armament") consisted of four 155-millimetre (6.1 in) triple-[gun turrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_turret "Gun turret") formerly used by the [_Mogami_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mogami-class_cruiser "Mogami-class cruiser")[cruisers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruiser "Cruiser"). They were equipped with six or seven [floatplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floatplane "Floatplane") to conduct reconnaissance.

Commissioned in mid-1942, _Musashi_ was modified to serve as the [flagship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship "Flagship") of the [Combined Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_Fleet "Combined Fleet"), and spent the rest of the year [working up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_nautical_terms_(M-Z)#working_up "Glossary of nautical terms (M-Z)"). The ship was transferred to [Truk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuuk_Lagoon "Chuuk Lagoon"), [Japan's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan") main wartime naval base in the [South Pacific theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War"), in early 1943 and [sortied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortie "Sortie") several times that year with the fleet in unsuccessful searches for [American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_United_States_during_World_War_II "Military history of the United States during World War II") forces. She was used to transfer forces and equipment between Japan and various occupied islands several times in 1944. [Torpedoed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo "Torpedo") in early 1944 by an American [submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine "Submarine"), _Musashi_ was forced to return to Japan for repairs, during which the navy greatly augmented her [anti-aircraft armament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare"). She was present during the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea "Battle of the Philippine Sea") in June, but did not come in contact with American surface forces. During the [Battle of Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leyte_Gulf "Battle of Leyte Gulf"), _Musashi_ was sunk by an estimated 19 torpedo and 17 bomb hits from American [carrier-based aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrier-based_aircraft "Carrier-based aircraft") on 24 October 1944. Over half of her crew was rescued. Her wreck was located in March 2015 by a team of researchers employed by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") co-founder [Paul Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen").

## Design and description

Main article: [_Yamato_-class battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamato-class_battleship "Yamato-class battleship")

Since the IJN anticipated it would be unable to produce as many ships as the United States, the _Yamato_-class ships with their great size and heavy armament were designed to be individually superior to American battleships.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-6)_Musashi_ had a length of 244 metres (800 ft 6 in)[between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars") and 263 metres (862 ft 10 in)[overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall"). She had a [waterline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterline "Waterline")[beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 38.9 metres (127 ft 7 in) and a [draught](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(ship) "Draft (ship)") of 10.86 metres (35 ft 8 in) at [deep load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_load "Deep load").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-s10-7) She [displaced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)")64,000 [long tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton "Long ton") (65,000[t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne")) at [standard load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_displacement#Standard_displacement "Standard displacement") and 71,659 long tons (72,809 t) at deep load. Her crew consisted of 2,500 officers and [ratings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_rating "Naval rating") in 1942, and about 2,800 in 1944.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-j8-8)

The battleship had four sets of [Kampon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Navy_Technical_Department "Imperial Japanese Navy Technical Department") geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine"), each of which drove one propeller shaft. The turbines were designed to produce a total of 150,000 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (110,000[kW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilowatt "Kilowatt")), using steam provided by 12 Kampon [water-tube boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water-tube_boiler "Water-tube boiler"), giving the ship a maximum speed of 27.5 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (50.9 km/h; 31.6 mph). She had a stowage capacity of 6,300 long tons (6,400 t) of [fuel oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuel_oil "Fuel oil"), giving a range of 7,200 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (13,300 km; 8,300 mi) at a speed of 16 knots (30 km/h; 18 mph).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-j8-8)

_Musashi_ seen from the bow, August 1942

_Musashi_'s [main battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_battery "Main battery") consisted of nine 45-[calibre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliber_(artillery) "Caliber (artillery)")[460-millimetre Type 94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/40_cm/45_Type_94 "40 cm/45 Type 94") guns mounted in three triple gun turrets, numbered from front to rear. The guns had a rate of fire of 1.5 to 2 rounds per minute.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-c8-9) The ship's [secondary battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_armament "Secondary armament") consisted of twelve 60-calibre [155-millimetre 3rd Year Type guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15.5_cm/60_3rd_Year_Type_naval_gun "15.5 cm/60 3rd Year Type naval gun") mounted in four triple turrets, one each fore and aft of the [superstructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstructure "Superstructure") and one on each side [amidships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amidships "Amidships"). These had become available once the _Mogami_-class cruisers were rearmed with [200-millimetre (7.9 in)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/20_cm/50_3rd_Year_Type_naval_gun "20 cm/50 3rd Year Type naval gun") guns.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-10) Heavy [anti-aircraft defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") was provided by a dozen 40-calibre [127-millimetre (5 in) Type 89](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12.7_cm/40_Type_89_naval_gun "12.7 cm/40 Type 89 naval gun")[dual-purpose guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-purpose_gun "Dual-purpose gun") in six twin turrets, three on each side of the superstructure. _Musashi_ also carried thirty-six [25-millimetre (1 in) Type 96](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_96_25_mm_AT/AA_Gun "Type 96 25 mm AT/AA Gun") light [anti-aircraft (AA) guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_gun "Anti-aircraft gun") in 12 triple-gun mounts, all mounted on the superstructure.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-s20-11) The ship was also provided with two twin mounts for the [licence-built](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Licence-built "Licence-built")[13.2-millimetre (0.52 in) Type 93](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13.2_mm_Hotchkiss_machine_gun "13.2 mm Hotchkiss machine gun") anti-aircraft [machine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_gun "Machine gun"), one on each side of the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_(nautical) "Bridge (nautical)").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-c8-9)

While the ship was under repair in April 1944, the two 155 mm [wing turrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing_turret "Wing turret") were removed and replaced with three triple 25 mm gun mounts each. A total of sixteen triple 25 mm mounts and twenty-five single mounts were added at that time, giving the ship a light AA armament of 115 guns.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

### Armour

The ship's waterline [armour belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belt_armor "Belt armor") was identical to [_Yamato_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Yamato "Japanese battleship Yamato")'s at 410 millimetres (16.1 in) thick and angled outwards 20 degrees at the top.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-USNTMJ-13) Below it was a [strake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strake "Strake") of armour that ranged in thickness from 270 to 200 millimetres (10.6 to 7.9 in) over the [magazines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magazine_(artillery)#Naval_magazines "Magazine (artillery)") and machinery spaces, respectively; it tapered to a thickness of 75 millimetres (3.0 in) at its bottom edge. The [deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deck_(ship) "Deck (ship)") armour ranged in thickness from 230 to 200 millimetres (9.1 to 7.9 in). The turrets were protected with an armour plate 650 millimetres (25.6 in) thick on the face, 250 millimetres (9.8 in) on the sides, and 270 millimetres on the roof. The [barbettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbette "Barbette") of the turrets were protected by armour 560 to 280 millimetres (22.0 to 11.0 in) thick, and the turrets of the 155 mm guns were protected by 50-millimetre (2.0 in) armour plates. The sides of the [conning tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conning_tower "Conning tower") were 500 millimetres (19.7 in) thick and its roof was 200 millimetres thick. Underneath the magazines were 50-to-80-millimetre (2.0 to 3.1 in) armour plates to protect the ship from [mine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine") damage. _Musashi_ contained 1,147 watertight compartments (1,065 underneath the armour deck, 82 above) to preserve [buoyancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buoyancy "Buoyancy") in the event of battle damage.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-14)

### Aircraft

_Musashi_ was fitted with two [catapults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_catapult "Aircraft catapult") on her [quarterdeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterdeck "Quarterdeck") and could stow up to seven [floatplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floatplane "Floatplane") in her below-decks [hangar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangar "Hangar"). The ship operated [Mitsubishi F1M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi_F1M "Mitsubishi F1M")[biplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biplane "Biplane") and [Aichi E13A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aichi_E13A "Aichi E13A")1 monoplanes and used a 6-tonne (5.9-long-ton), stern-mounted [crane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crane_(machine) "Crane (machine)") for recovery.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-15)

### Fire control and sensors

The ship was equipped with four 15-metre (49 ft 3 in)[rangefinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangefinding_telemeter "Rangefinding telemeter"), one atop her forward superstructure and one in each of her main gun turrets, and another 10-metre (32 ft 10 in) unit atop her rear superstructure. Each 15.5-centimetre (6.1 in) gun turret was equipped with an 8-metre (26 ft 3 in) rangefinder. Low-angle fire was controlled by two Type 98 [fire-control directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-control_director "Fire-control director") mounted above the rangefinders on the superstructure. Type 94 high-angle directors controlled the 127 mm AA guns, with Type 95 short-range directors for the 25 mm AA guns.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-16)

_Musashi_ was built with a Type 0 [hydrophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrophone "Hydrophone") system in her bow, usable only while stationary or at low speed.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-17) In September 1942, a [Type 21 air-search radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Japanese_World_War_II_radar#Shipborne_radar "List of Japanese World War II radar") was installed on the roof of the 15-metre rangefinder at the top of the forward superstructure. Two Type 22 surface-search radars were installed on the forward superstructure in July 1943. During repairs in April 1944, the Type 21 radar was replaced by a more modern version, and a Type 13 [early-warning radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early-warning_radar "Early-warning radar") was also fitted.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

## Construction

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Musashi1944.png/250px-Musashi1944.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Musashi1944.png)

_Musashi_ as she appeared in mid-1944

To cope with _Musashi_'s great size and weight, the construction [slipway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slipway "Slipway") was reinforced, nearby workshops were expanded, and two [floating cranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crane_(machine)#Floating "Crane (machine)") were built. The ship's [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel") was laid down on 29 March 1938 at [Mitsubishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi "Mitsubishi")'s [Nagasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagasaki "Nagasaki") shipyard, and was designated "Battleship No. 2". Throughout construction, a large curtain made of hemp rope weighing 408 t (450 short tons) prevented outsiders from viewing construction.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-Y29-19)[[N 2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-21)

[Launching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Launch_(ship) "Launch (ship)") the _Musashi_ also presented challenges. The ship's 4-metre (13 ft 1 in) thick launch platform, made of nine 44 cm (17 in)[Douglas fir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_fir "Douglas fir") planks bolted together, took two years to assemble (from keel-laying in March 1938) because of the difficulty in drilling perfectly straight bolt holes through 4 metres of fresh timber. The problem of slowing and stopping the massive hull once inside the narrow Nagasaki Harbour was met by attaching 570 tonnes (560 long tons) of heavy chains on both sides of the hull to create dragging resistance in the water. The launch was concealed by measures that included a citywide [air-raid drill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_defense "Civil defense") staged on launch day to keep people inside their homes. _Musashi_ was launched on 1 November 1940, coming to a stop only 1 metre (3.3 ft) further than the hull's expected 220 metres (720 ft) travel distance across the harbour. The entry of such a large mass into the water caused a 120-centimetre-tall (3 ft 11 in) wave, which swept the harbour and local rivers, flooding homes and capsizing small fishing boats.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-22)_Musashi_ was [fitted out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitting-out "Fitting-out") at nearby [Sasebo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sasebo,_Nagasaki "Sasebo, Nagasaki"), with [Captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(naval) "Captain (naval)")[Kaoru Arima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaoru_Arima "Kaoru Arima") assigned as her commanding officer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

Towards the end of fitting out, the ship's flagship facilities, including those on the [bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship's_bridge "Ship's bridge") and in the admiral's [cabins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabin_(ship) "Cabin (ship)"), were modified to satisfy Combined Fleet's desire to have the ship equipped as the primary flagship of the commander-in-chief, as her [sister ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_ship "Sister ship")_Yamato_ was too far along for such changes. These alterations, along with improvements in the secondary battery armour, pushed back completion and pre-handover testing of _Musashi_ by two months, to August 1942.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-23)

## Service

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Japanese_battleships_Yamato_and_Musashi_moored_in_Truk_Lagoon%2C_in_1943_%28L42-08.06.02%29.jpg/250px-Japanese_battleships_Yamato_and_Musashi_moored_in_Truk_Lagoon%2C_in_1943_%28L42-08.06.02%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Japanese_battleships_Yamato_and_Musashi_moored_in_Truk_Lagoon,_in_1943_(L42-08.06.02).jpg)

_Musashi_ (right) and _[Yamato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_battleship\_Yamato "Japanese battleship Yamato")_ in [Truk Lagoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuuk_Lagoon "Chuuk Lagoon") in early 1943

_Musashi_ was commissioned at Nagasaki on 5 August 1942, and assigned to the 1st Battleship Division, together with _Yamato_, [_Nagato_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Nagato "Japanese battleship Nagato") and [_Mutsu_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Mutsu "Japanese battleship Mutsu").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-24) Beginning five days later, the ship conducted machinery and aircraft-handling trials near [Hashirajima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hashirajima "Hashirajima"). Her secondary armament of twelve 127 mm guns, 12 triple 25 mm gun mounts, and four 13.2 mm (0.52 in) anti-aircraft machine guns was fitted 3–28 September 1942 at Kure, as well as a Type 21 radar. The ship was working up for the rest of the year. Arima was promoted to [rear admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_admiral "Rear admiral") on 1 November.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

_Musashi_ was assigned to the [Combined Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Combined_Fleet "Japanese Combined Fleet"), commanded by Admiral [Isoroku Yamamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isoroku_Yamamoto "Isoroku Yamamoto"), on 15 January 1943[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-w6-25) and sailed for Truk three days later, arriving on 22 January. On 11 February, she replaced her sister ship _Yamato_ as the fleet's flagship. On 3 April, Yamamoto left _Musashi_ and flew to [Rabaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabaul "Rabaul"), [New Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Britain "New Britain") to personally direct ["Operation _I-Go_"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_I-Go "Operation I-Go"), a Japanese aerial offensive in the [Solomon Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_Islands "Solomon Islands"). His orders were intercepted and deciphered by [Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magic_(cryptography) "Magic (cryptography)"), and American [Lockheed P-38 Lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_P-38_Lightning "Lockheed P-38 Lightning") fighters shot down his transport aircraft and killed him in [Operation Vengeance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Vengeance "Operation Vengeance") while he was en route from New Britain to Ballale, [Bougainville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bougainville_Island "Bougainville Island"). On 23 April, his [cremated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cremation "Cremation") remains were flown back to Truk and placed in his cabin on board _Musashi_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

On 17 May, in response to American [attacks on Attu Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Attu "Battle of Attu"), _Musashi_—together with the [aircraft carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier")[_Hiyō_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Hiy%C5%8D "Japanese aircraft carrier Hiyō"), two [heavy cruisers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_cruiser "Heavy cruiser"), and nine [destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer")—[sortied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortie "Sortie") to the northern Pacific. When no contact was made with American forces, the ships sailed to Kure on 23 May, where Yamamoto's ashes were taken from the vessel in preparation for a formal [state funeral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_funeral "State funeral"). Immediately afterwards, _Musashi_'s task force was significantly reinforced to counterattack American naval forces off Attu, but the island was captured before the force could intervene. On 9 June, Arima was relieved by Captain [Keizō Komura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiz%C5%8D_Komura "Keizō Komura"). On 24 June, while being overhauled at [Yokosuka Naval Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokosuka_Naval_Arsenal "Yokosuka Naval Arsenal"), _Musashi_ was visited by [Emperor Hirohito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Hirohito "Emperor Hirohito") and high-ranking naval officers. From 1 to 8 July, the ship was fitted with a pair of Type 22 radars at Kure.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12) She sailed for Truk on 30 July and arrived there six days later, where she resumed her position as fleet flagship for Admiral [Mineichi Koga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineichi_Koga "Mineichi Koga").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-w6-25)

In mid-October, in response to suspicions of planned American raids on [Wake Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Island "Wake Island"), _Musashi_ led a large fleet—three carriers, six battleships, and 11 cruisers—to intercept American forces, but failed to make contact and returned to Truk on 26 October. She spent the remainder of 1943 in Truk Lagoon. Komura was promoted to rear admiral on 1 November and transferred to the [3rd Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_Fleet_(Imperial_Japanese_Navy) "3rd Fleet (Imperial Japanese Navy)") on 7 December as [chief of staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_staff "Chief of staff"); Captain Bunji Asakura assumed command of _Musashi_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/%E5%B3%B6%E6%9D%91%E4%BF%A1%E6%94%BF5.jpg/250px-%E5%B3%B6%E6%9D%91%E4%BF%A1%E6%94%BF5.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%E5%B3%B6%E6%9D%91%E4%BF%A1%E6%94%BF5.jpg)

[Emperor Hirohito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Hirohito "Emperor Hirohito") and his staff on board _Musashi_, 24 June 1943. Visible in the background are two pairs of twin 127 mm (5 in) DP guns and a triple 25 mm (1 in) AA gun.

The ship remained in Truk Lagoon until 10 February 1944, when she returned to Yokosuka. On 24 February, _Musashi_ sailed for [Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau "Palau"), carrying one [Imperial Japanese Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Army "Imperial Japanese Army")[battalion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battalion "Battalion") and another of [Special Naval Landing Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Naval_Landing_Force "Special Naval Landing Force") and their equipment. After losing most of her deck cargo in a [typhoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon "Typhoon"), she arrived at Palau on 29 February and remained there for the next month. On 29 March, _Musashi_ departed Palau under cover of darkness to avoid an expected air raid, and encountered the submarine [USS _Tunny_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Tunny_(SS-282) "USS Tunny (SS-282)"), which fired six torpedoes at the battleship; five of them missed, but the sixth blew a hole 5.8 metres (19 ft) in diameter near the bow, flooding her with 3,000 tonnes of water.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-stille42-26) The torpedo hit killed seven crewmen and wounded another eleven. After temporary repairs, _Musashi_ sailed for Japan later that night and arrived at [Kure Naval Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kure_Naval_Arsenal "Kure Naval Arsenal") on 3 April. From 10 to 22 April, she was repaired, while her anti-aircraft armament was substantially increased in the space freed up by removal of the beam-mounted 155-millimetre (6.1 in) triple turrets. When she undocked on 22 April, the ship's secondary battery comprised six 15.5 cm guns, twenty-four 12.7 cm guns, one hundred and thirty 25 mm guns, and four 13.2 mm machine guns. She also received new radars (which were still primitive compared to American equipment)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-27) and [depth-charge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") rails on her [fantail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poop_deck "Poop deck").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

In May 1944, Asakura was promoted to rear admiral; _Musashi_ departed Kure for [Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okinawa_Prefecture "Okinawa Prefecture") on 10 May, then for [Tawi-Tawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tawi-Tawi "Tawi-Tawi") on 12 May. She was assigned to the [1st Mobile Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Mobile_Fleet_(Imperial_Japanese_Navy) "1st Mobile Fleet (Imperial Japanese Navy)"), under the command of [Vice Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Admiral "Vice Admiral")[Jisaburō Ozawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jisabur%C5%8D_Ozawa "Jisaburō Ozawa"), with her sister ship. On 10 June, the battleships departed Tawi-Tawi for [Batjan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batjan "Batjan") under the command of Vice Admiral [Matome Ugaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matome_Ugaki "Matome Ugaki"), in preparation for [Operation Kon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Kon?action=edit&redlink=1 "Operation Kon (page does not exist)"), a planned counterattack against the American [invasion of Biak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Biak "Battle of Biak"). Two days later, when word reached Ugaki of American attacks on [Saipan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saipan "Saipan"), his force was diverted to the [Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_Islands "Mariana Islands"). After they rendezvoused with Ozawa's main force on 16 June, the battleships were assigned to Vice Admiral [Takeo Kurita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Takeo_Kurita "Takeo Kurita")'s [2nd Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Fleet_(Imperial_Japanese_Navy) "2nd Fleet (Imperial Japanese Navy)"). During the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea "Battle of the Philippine Sea"), _Musashi_ was not attacked.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-stille42-26) Following Japan's disastrous defeat in the battle (also known as the "Great Marianas Turkey Shoot"), the Second Fleet returned to Japan. On 8 July, _Musashi_ and her sister embarked 3,522 men and equipment of the Army's [106th Infantry Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/106th_Infantry_Regiment_(Japan)?action=edit&redlink=1 "106th Infantry Regiment (Japan) (page does not exist)") of the [49th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/49th_Infantry_Division_(Imperial_Japanese_Army) "49th Infantry Division (Imperial Japanese Army)") and sailed for [Lingga Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingga_Island "Lingga Island"), where they arrived on 17 July.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

### Battle of Leyte Gulf

Main article: [Battle of Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leyte_Gulf "Battle of Leyte Gulf")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Bf8951fe9f6830e390472cf11cc61593_%281%29.jpg/250px-Bf8951fe9f6830e390472cf11cc61593_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bf8951fe9f6830e390472cf11cc61593_(1).jpg)

_Musashi_ (right) and _Yamato_ anchored in Brunei shortly before the [battle of Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leyte_Gulf "Battle of Leyte Gulf"), 21 October 1944

Captain [Toshihira Inoguchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toshihira_Inoguchi "Toshihira Inoguchi") relieved Asakura in command of _Musashi_ on 12 August 1944 and was promoted to rear admiral on 15 October.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12) Three days later, the ship sailed for [Brunei Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunei_Bay "Brunei Bay"), Borneo to join the main Japanese fleet in preparation for "Operation _Sho_-1", the planned counterattack against the American landings at Leyte. The Japanese plan called for Ozawa's carrier forces to lure the American carrier fleets north of Leyte so that Kurita's 1st Diversion Force (also known as the Central Force) could enter [Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyte_Gulf "Leyte Gulf") and destroy American forces landing on the island. _Musashi_, together with the rest of Kurita's force, departed Brunei for the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines") on 22 October.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-28)

The following day, the submarine [USS _Dace_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Dace_(SS-247) "USS Dace (SS-247)") torpedoed and sank the heavy cruiser [_Maya_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_cruiser_Maya "Japanese cruiser Maya") near [Palawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palawan_(island) "Palawan (island)"). The destroyer [_Akishimo_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_destroyer_Akishimo "Japanese destroyer Akishimo") rescued 769 survivors and transferred them to _Musashi_ later in the day.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-29)

#### Loss at Sibuyan Sea

On 24 October, while transiting the [Sibuyan Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sibuyan_Sea "Sibuyan Sea"), Kurita's ships were spotted by a reconnaissance aircraft from the [fleet carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_carrier "Fleet carrier")[USS _Intrepid_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Intrepid_(CV-11) "USS Intrepid (CV-11)"). Just over two hours later, the battleship was attacked by eight [Curtiss SB2C Helldiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtiss_SB2C_Helldiver "Curtiss SB2C Helldiver")[dive bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dive_bomber "Dive bomber") from _Intrepid_ at 10:27. One 230-kilogram (500 lb) bomb struck the roof of Turret No. 1, failing to penetrate. Two minutes later, _Musashi_ was struck starboard amidships by a torpedo from a [Grumman TBF Avenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_TBF_Avenger "Grumman TBF Avenger"), also from _Intrepid_. The ship took on 3,000 tonnes of water and a 5.5-degree [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_(watercraft) "List (watercraft)") to starboard that was later reduced to 1 degree by counterflooding compartments on the opposite side. During this attack, two Avengers were shot down.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Sibuyan_Sea-battleship.jpg/250px-Sibuyan_Sea-battleship.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sibuyan_Sea-battleship.jpg)

_Musashi_ taking a torpedo hit early into the battle, 24 October 1944

An hour and a half later, another eight Helldivers from _Intrepid_ attacked _Musashi_ again. One bomb hit the upper deck and failed to detonate; another hit the port side of the deck and penetrated two upper decks before exploding above one of the engine rooms. Fragments broke a steam pipe in the engine room and forced its abandonment, as well as that of the adjacent boiler room. Power was lost to the port inboard propeller shaft and the ship's speed dropped to 22 knots (41 km/h; 25 mph). Anti-aircraft fire shot down two Helldivers during this attack. Three minutes later, nine Avengers attacked from both sides of the ship, scoring three torpedo hits on the port side. One hit abreast Turret No. 1, the second flooded a hydraulic machinery room, forcing the main turrets to switch over to auxiliary hydraulic pumps, and the third flooded another engine room. More counterflooding reduced the list to one degree to port, but the amount of flooding reduced the ship's forward [freeboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freeboard_(nautical) "Freeboard (nautical)") by 1.8 metres (6 ft). During this attack, _Musashi_ fired _[sanshikidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beehive\_(anti-aircraft\_shell) "Beehive (anti-aircraft shell)")_ anti-aircraft shells from her main armament; one shell detonated in the middle gun of Turret No. 1, possibly because of a bomb fragment in the barrel, and wrecked the turret's elevating machinery.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Japanese_battleship_Musashi_and_a_destroyer_under_attack_in_the_Sibuyan_Sea%2C_24_October_1944_%28NH_63432%29.jpg/250px-Japanese_battleship_Musashi_and_a_destroyer_under_attack_in_the_Sibuyan_Sea%2C_24_October_1944_%28NH_63432%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Japanese_battleship_Musashi_and_a_destroyer_under_attack_in_the_Sibuyan_Sea,_24_October_1944_(NH_63432).jpg)

_Musashi_ heavily damaged and still under attack; her draft has noticeably risen nearly to the deck. The destroyer _[Kiyoshimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_destroyer\_Kiyoshimo "Japanese destroyer Kiyoshimo")_ is seen being strafed behind her.

At 13:31, the ship was attacked by 29 aircraft from fleet carriers [_Essex_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Essex_(CV-9) "USS Essex (CV-9)") and [_Lexington_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Lexington_(CV-16) "USS Lexington (CV-16)"). Two [Grumman F6F Hellcat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_F6F_Hellcat "Grumman F6F Hellcat") fighters [strafed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafe "Strafe") the ship's deck and Helldivers scored four more bomb hits near her forward turrets. _Musashi_ was hit by four more torpedoes, three of which were forward of Turret No. 1, causing extensive flooding. The ship was now listing one degree to starboard, and had taken on so much water that her bow was now down 4 metres (13 ft) and her speed had been reduced to 20 knots (37 km/h; 23 mph). Two hours later, nine Helldivers from [_Enterprise_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Enterprise_(CV-6) "USS Enterprise (CV-6)") attacked with 450-kilogram (1,000 lb)[armour-piercing bombs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armor-piercing_shot_and_shell "Armor-piercing shot and shell") and scored four hits which killed the entire forward damage control team, before another wave of _Enterprise_ aircraft hit _Musashi_ with three more torpedoes, opening up her starboard bow and reducing her speed to 13 knots (24 km/h; 15 mph).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-30) At 15:25, _Musashi_ was attacked by 37 aircraft from _Intrepid_, the fleet carrier [_Franklin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Franklin_(CV-13) "USS Franklin (CV-13)") and the [light carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_carrier "Light carrier")[_Cabot_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Cabot_(CVL-28) "USS Cabot (CVL-28)"). The ship was hit by 13 bombs and 11 more torpedoes during this attack, for a loss of three Avengers and three Helldivers. Her speed was reduced to 6 knots (11 km/h; 6.9 mph), her main [steering engine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steering_engine "Steering engine") was temporarily knocked out and her [rudder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudder "Rudder") was briefly jammed 15 degrees to port. Counterflooding reduced her list to six degrees to port from its previous maximum of ten degrees. _Musashi_ had been struck by an estimated total of 19 torpedoes and 17 bombs.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12)[[N 3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-33)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Japanese_battleship_Musashi_on_24_October_1944%2C_down_at_the_bow_and_sinking_%28NH_63434%29.jpg/250px-Japanese_battleship_Musashi_on_24_October_1944%2C_down_at_the_bow_and_sinking_%28NH_63434%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Japanese_battleship_Musashi_on_24_October_1944,_down_at_the_bow_and_sinking_(NH_63434).jpg)

_Musashi_ down by the bow after the air attacks, shortly before her sinking

Kurita left _Musashi_ to fend for herself at 15:30, and encountered her again at 16:21 after reversing course. The ship was headed north, with a list of 10 degrees to port, down 8 metres (26 ft) at the bow with her [forecastle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forecastle "Forecastle") awash. He detailed a heavy cruiser and two destroyers to escort her while frantic efforts were made to correct her list, including flooding another engine room and some boiler rooms. Her engines stopped before she could be [beached](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beaching_(nautical) "Beaching (nautical)"). At 19:15, her list reached 12 degrees and her crew was ordered to prepare to abandon ship, which they did fifteen minutes later when the list reached 30 degrees. _Musashi_ capsized at 19:36 and sank in 1,350 metres (4,430 ft) of water at [13°07′N 122°32′E / 13.117°N 122.533°E / 13.117; 122.533](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=Japanese_battleship_Musashi&params=13_07_N_122_32_E_).[[N 4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-34) Inoguchi chose to go down with his ship; 1,376 of her 2,399-man crew were rescued by the destroyers _[Kiyoshimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_destroyer\_Kiyoshimo "Japanese destroyer Kiyoshimo")_ and _[Hamakaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese\_destroyer\_Hamakaze\_(1940) "Japanese destroyer Hamakaze (1940)")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-35) About half of her survivors were evacuated to Japan, and the rest took part in the defence of the Philippines.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-cfrecord-12) The destroyer [_Shimakaze_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_destroyer_Shimakaze_(1942) "Japanese destroyer Shimakaze (1942)") rescued 635 of _Maya_'s survivors from _Musashi_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-36)

## Wreck

### Discovery

For over 70 years after her sinking, various attempts were made by [shipwreck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipwreck "Shipwreck") hunters to locate the wreck of the Japanese battleship, but none succeeded. _Musashi_, like other Japanese warships, did not have its name on its sides, making it more difficult for divers and shipwreck hunters to find her. A research team sponsored by [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft") co-founder [Paul Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Allen "Paul Allen") eventually found her after eight years of searching for the wreck, going through various historical records in different countries, and deploying the high-tech [yacht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yacht "Yacht")[_Octopus_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus_(yacht) "Octopus (yacht)") and a [remotely operated vehicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remotely_operated_underwater_vehicle "Remotely operated underwater vehicle") to aid in their search. In March 2015, Allen announced that the team had found _Musashi_ under the Sibuyan Sea, some 900 metres (3,000 ft) beneath the surface.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-hist-37)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-Allen_discovers_wreck_of_Japan's_biggest_warship_Musashi-38)

The ship had been thought to have sunk in one piece; in reality, it exploded underwater,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-39) scattering debris across the ocean floor. The bow section from the number one barbette forward is upright on the sea floor, while the stern is upside down. The forward superstructure and funnel is detached from the rest of the ship and lies on its port side.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-Allen2015-40) In the live streaming video tour conducted by the expedition team, a mount for the seal of the Imperial Japanese Navy—a [chrysanthemum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysanthemum "Chrysanthemum") made out of [teak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teak "Teak"), long rotted away—can be seen amid the debris. The video also showed damage made by U.S. torpedoes, including a warped bow and hits under the ship's main gun.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-Allen2015-40) Other items found in the area of the wreck, as well as other features found inside, led maritime experts to claim with 90% certainty that the wreck was _Musashi_.

To further confirm the identity of the wreck, Shigeru Nakajima, an electrical technician on _Musashi_ who survived by jumping overboard after the order to abandon ship was given, told the [Associated Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press "Associated Press") that he was "certain" that the wreck was _Musashi_ upon seeing its anchor and the imperial seal mount. He also expressed his gratitude to the expedition team for having located the shipwreck.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-hist-37)

### Preservation and protection

The discovery of the wreck beneath the surface of the Sibuyan Sea raised issues in the Philippines because the provincial government of [Romblon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romblon "Romblon"), which has jurisdiction over the shipwreck site, and the [Philippine Coast Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Coast_Guard "Philippine Coast Guard") were unaware that Allen and his team had an ongoing expedition in the area, though Governor Eduardo Firmalo publicly welcomed discovery of the ship. In response to the find, the Philippine Coast Guard stated that foreign-owned vessels need clearance from the Philippine Foreign Affairs Department, the Customs Bureau, and the Immigration Bureau before entering Philippine waters.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-abs-41)

Although discovering the shipwreck was very important to the Japanese people because of the presence aboard of over 1,000 Japanese sailors' remains, the [National Museum of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_the_Philippines "National Museum of the Philippines") stated that "any further activity [pertaining to the shipwreck would] be governed by established rules and regulations." The Museum pointed out that the wreck site of _Musashi_, as stated by the law, is considered an archaeological site under Romblon's jurisdiction, and was "giving priority to verifying the discovery, obtaining and sharing key information, facilitating the protection and preservation of the site, and formulating appropriate next steps."[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Musashi#cite_note-abs-41)

Battleship NJ History

BB62 was built at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, and launched December 7, 1942—just a year after the Pearl Harbor Attack brought America into WWII.

NEW JERSEY (BB-62) was decommissioned for the fourth and final time on February 8, 1991 in Long Beach, California and later towed to Bremerton, Washington where she resided until heading home to New Jersey. She was officially stricken from the Navy list on February 12, 1995 but was then ordered reinstated by an order of congress as a mobilization asset under Bill 1024 section 1011. On January 4, 1999 NEW JERSEY was again stricken from the Navy list and IOWA replaced her as a mobilization asset. On September 12, 1999 NEW JERSEY began her Final Voyage home from Bremerton, where she had rested in mothballs for the last 8 years. On November 11th, she arrived at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard. Since that time, she has been restored, opened and established as an educational museum and a tribute to the brave sailors who served on her during her long and distinguished career. The Battleship New Jersey opened as a Museum and Memorial in October 2001.
