She served as a tourist attraction, logging about 250,000 visitors per year,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-bsimof-78) who came to view the "surrender deck" where a bronze plaque memorialized the spot ([35°21′17″N 139°45′36″E / 35.3547°N 139.76°E / 35.3547; 139.76](https://geohack.toolforge.org/geohack.php?pagename=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&params=35.3547_N_139.76_E_)) in Tokyo Bay where Japan surrendered to the Allies. The accompanying historical display included copies of the surrender documents and photos.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-mqnawe-75) Nearly thirty years passed before _Missouri_ returned to active duty.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell238%E2%80%93246-76)

### Reactivation (1984–1990)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reactivation (1984–1990)")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Missouri_Recomissioned_%281986%29.jpg/250px-Missouri_Recomissioned_%281986%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Missouri_Recomissioned_(1986).jpg)

Crewmen [manning the rails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manning_the_rails "Manning the rails") of _Missouri_ during her recommissioning ceremony in San Francisco.

Under the [Reagan Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")'s program to build a [600-ship Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/600-ship_Navy "600-ship Navy"), led by Secretary of the Navy [John F. Lehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Lehman "John F. Lehman"), _Missouri_ was reactivated and towed by the [salvage ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salvage_ship "Salvage ship")[_Beaufort_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Beaufort_(ATS-2) "USS Beaufort (ATS-2)") to the Long Beach Naval Yard in the summer of 1984 to undergo modernization in advance of her scheduled recommissioning.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-bsimof-78) In preparation for the move, a skeleton crew of 20 spent three weeks working 12 to 16-hour days preparing the battleship for her tow.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-79)

Over the next several months, the ship had her obsolete armament removed: 20 mm and 40 mm AA guns, their directors, and four of her ten 5-inch gun mounts. Installed in their place on the superstructure were four Mk 141 quad cell launchers for 16 [RGM-84 Harpoon anti-ship missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpoon_(missile) "Harpoon (missile)"), eight Mk 143 Armored Box Launcher mounts for 32 [BGM-109 Tomahawk cruise missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tomahawk_(missile_family) "Tomahawk (missile family)"), and a quartet of 20 mm [Phalanx CIWS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phalanx_CIWS "Phalanx CIWS")[rotary cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotary_cannon "Rotary cannon") for defense against enemy [anti-ship missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-ship_missile "Anti-ship missile") and enemy aircraft. She also received upgrades to radar and fire-control systems for her guns and missiles, and improved [electronic warfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_warfare "Electronic warfare") capabilities. Additions included an [AN/SPS-49](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/SPS-49 "AN/SPS-49") early-warning radar and an [AN/SPS-67](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/SPS-67 "AN/SPS-67") surface-search radar[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell393-80) while the SPS-8 radar and the mainmast were removed.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall143-81) The added missile capacity necessitated additional fire-support systems to launch and guide the ordnance. To fire the Harpoon anti-ship missiles, the ship was equipped with the SWG-1 fire-control system. _Missouri_ was also outfitted with the [AN/SLQ-25 Nixie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/SLQ-25_Nixie "AN/SLQ-25 Nixie") to be used as a decoy against enemy torpedoes, an [AN/SLQ-32 Electronic Warfare Suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/SLQ-32_Electronic_Warfare_Suite "AN/SLQ-32 Electronic Warfare Suite") electronic-warfare system that can detect, jam, and deceive an opponent's radar and a [Mark 36 SRBOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_36_SRBOC "Mark 36 SRBOC") system to fire [chaff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaff_(countermeasure) "Chaff (countermeasure)") rockets intended to confuse enemy missiles.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESharpe1991732-82) The ship's crew now consisted of 65 officers and 1,450 enlisted men.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall159-7)

During the modernization the ship's 800 lb (360 kg) bell, which had been removed from the battleship and sent to [Jefferson City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_City,_Missouri "Jefferson City, Missouri") for sesquicentennial celebrations in the state, was formally returned to the battleship in advance of her recommissioning.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-83)_Missouri_ was formally recommissioned in San Francisco on 10 May 1986 with Captain Albert Kaiss in command. "This is a day to celebrate the rebirth of American sea power", Secretary of Defense [Caspar Weinberger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caspar_Weinberger "Caspar Weinberger") told an audience of 10,000 at the recommissioning ceremony, instructing the crew to "listen for the footsteps of those who have gone before you. They speak to you of honor and the importance of duty. They remind you of your own traditions."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-chinfo-84) Margaret Truman gave a short speech especially aimed at the ship's crew, which ended with "now take care of my baby." Her remarks were met with rounds of applause from the crew.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-85)

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/AO-146_refuel_CV-63_BB-63_1986.jpeg/250px-AO-146_refuel_CV-63_BB-63_1986.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:AO-146_refuel_CV-63_BB-63_1986.jpeg)

_Missouri_ performing an [underway replenishment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Underway_replenishment "Underway replenishment") with [_Kitty Hawk_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Kitty_Hawk_(CV-63) "USS Kitty Hawk (CV-63)") from the [MSC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Sealift_Command "Military Sealift Command") ship [USNS _Kawishiwi_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USNS_Kawishiwi "USNS Kawishiwi").

Only briefly in command, Kaiss was relieved by Captain James A. Carney on 20 June.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell389-62) Three months later _Missouri_ departed from her new home port of [Long Beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Station_Long_Beach "Naval Station Long Beach") for an around-the-world cruise, visiting Pearl Harbor Hawaii; [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), [Hobart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart "Hobart"), and [Perth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perth "Perth"), Australia; [Diego Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diego_Garcia "Diego Garcia"); the [Suez Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Canal "Suez Canal"); [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey; [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples "Naples"), Italy; [Rota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rota,_Andalusia "Rota, Andalusia"), Spain; [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal; and the [Panama Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal "Panama Canal"). _Missouri_ became the first American battleship to [circumnavigate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumnavigation "Circumnavigation") the globe since [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt")'s "[Great White Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_White_Fleet "Great White Fleet")" 80 years before—a fleet which included the first battleship named [USS _Missouri_(BB-11)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-11) "USS Missouri (BB-11)").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

The ship returned to the United States via Diego Garcia, Australia, and Hawaii in early 1988. **USS _Missouri_** (**BB-63**) is an [_Iowa_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa-class_battleship "Iowa-class battleship")[battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battleship "Battleship") built for the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy") (USN) in the 1940s and is now a [museum ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_ship "Museum ship"). Completed in 1944, she is the last battleship [commissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning "Ship commissioning") by the United States. The ship was assigned to the [Pacific Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), where she participated in the Battles of [Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Iwo_Jima "Battle of Iwo Jima") and [Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Okinawa "Battle of Okinawa") and shelled the [Japanese home islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_archipelago "Japanese archipelago"). Her [quarterdeck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterdeck "Quarterdeck") was the site where the [Japanese Instrument of Surrender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Instrument_of_Surrender "Japanese Instrument of Surrender") was signed, officially [ending World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_World_War_II_in_Asia "End of World War II in Asia").

After World War II, _Missouri_ served in various diplomatic, [show of force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Show_of_force "Show of force") and training missions. In 1950, the ship [ran aground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_USS_Missouri_grounding "1950 USS Missouri grounding") during [high tide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_tide "High tide") in [Chesapeake Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay "Chesapeake Bay") and after great effort was re-floated several weeks later. She later fought in the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") during two tours between 1950 and 1953. _Missouri_ was the first American battleship to arrive in Korean waters and served as the [flagship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship "Flagship") for several [admirals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral "Admiral"). The battleship took part in numerous shore bombardment operations and also served in a [screening role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screening_(tactical) "Screening (tactical)") for [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier"). _Missouri_ was [decommissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning#Ship_decommissioning "Ship commissioning") in 1955 and transferred to the [reserve fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_reserve_fleets "United States Navy reserve fleets") (also known as the "Mothball Fleet").

_Missouri_ was [reactivated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_battleship_retirement_debate "United States battleship retirement debate") and modernized in 1984 as part of the [600-ship Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/600-ship_Navy "600-ship Navy") plan. [Cruise missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruise_missile "Cruise missile") and [anti-ship missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-ship_missile "Anti-ship missile") launchers were added along with updated electronics. The ship served in the [Persian Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf") escorting [oil tankers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_tanker "Oil tanker") during threats from Iran, often while keeping her [fire-control systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-control_system "Fire-control system") trained on land-based Iranian missile launchers. She served in [Operation Desert Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Desert_Storm "Operation Desert Storm") in 1991 including providing fire support.

_Missouri_ was again decommissioned in 1992, but remained on the [Naval Vessel Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Vessel_Register "Naval Vessel Register") until her name was struck in 1995. In 1998, she was donated to the USS _Missouri_ Memorial Association and became a museum ship at [Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor "Pearl Harbor"), Hawaii.

## Background and description

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and description")]

Main articles: [Iowa-class battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa-class_battleship "Iowa-class battleship") and [Armament of the Iowa-class battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armament_of_the_Iowa-class_battleship "Armament of the Iowa-class battleship")

The _Iowa_ class of [fast battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_battleship "Fast battleship") was designed in the late 1930s in response to the [US Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Navy "US Navy")'s expectations for a future war with the [Empire of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan"). The last battleships to be built by the United States, they were also the US Navy's largest and fastest vessels of the type.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_198099-3) American officers preferred comparatively slow but heavily armed and armored battleships, but Navy planners determined that such a fleet would have difficulty in bringing the faster Japanese fleet to battle, particularly the [_Kongō_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kong%C5%8D-class_battlecruiser "Kongō-class battlecruiser")[battlecruisers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battlecruiser "Battlecruiser") and the [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier") of the [1st Air Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Air_Fleet "1st Air Fleet"). Design studies prepared during the development of the earlier [_North Carolina_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina-class_battleship "North Carolina-class battleship") and [_South Dakota_ classes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dakota-class_battleship_(1939) "South Dakota-class battleship (1939)") demonstrated the difficulty in resolving the desires of fleet officers with those of the planning staff within the [displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") limits imposed by the [Washington Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Naval_Treaty "Washington Naval Treaty") system, which had governed [capital ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_ship "Capital ship") construction since 1923. An escalator clause in the [Second London Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_London_Naval_Treaty "Second London Naval Treaty") of 1936 allowed an increase from 35,000 [long tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton "Long ton") (36,000[t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne")) to 45,000 long tons (46,000 t) in the event that any member nation refused to sign the treaty, which Japan refused to do.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985306%E2%80%93307-4)

_Missouri_ is 887 feet 3 inches (270.4 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and is 860 feet (262.1 m) long at the [waterline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterline "Waterline"). The ship has a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 108 ft 2 in (33 m) and a [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 37 ft 9 in (11.5 m) at her [full combat load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full-load_displacement "Full-load displacement") of 57,540 long tons (58,460 t).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall157-5) The _Iowa_-class ships are powered by four [General Electric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric "General Electric") geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine"), each driving one [screw propeller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screw_propeller "Screw propeller") using steam provided by eight oil-fired [Babcock & Wilcox boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babcock_&_Wilcox_boiler "Babcock & Wilcox boiler"). Rated at 212,000 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (158,000[kW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilowatt "Kilowatt")), the turbines were designed to give a top speed of 32.5 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (60.2 km/h; 37.4 mph), but were built to handle a 20 percent overload. None of the _Iowa_ s ever ran [speed trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_trials "Sea trials") in deep water, but the [Bureau of Ships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Ships "Bureau of Ships") estimated that they could reach a speed of about 34 knots (63 km/h; 39 mph) from 225,000 shp (168,000 kW) at a light displacement of 51,209 long tons (52,031 t). The ships had a designed cruising range of 15,000 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (28,000 km; 17,000 mi) at a speed of 15 knots (28 km/h; 17 mph), although the [_New Jersey_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_New_Jersey_(BB-62) "USS New Jersey (BB-62)")'s fuel consumption figures during her sea trials suggest that her range was at least 20,150 nmi (37,320 km; 23,190 mi) at that cruising speed. Their designed crew numbered 117 officers and 1,804[enlisted men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enlisted_men "Enlisted men") which had greatly increased by the end of the war in 1945.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985317,_319,_323,_449-6)_Missouri_'s crew at that time numbered 189 officers and 2,978 sailors.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall159-7)

### Armament, fire control, sensors and aircraft

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Armament, fire control, sensors and aircraft")]

The [main battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_battery "Main battery") of the _Iowa_-class ships consisted of nine [16 in (406 mm)/50 caliber Mark 7 guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16-inch/50-caliber_Mark_7_gun "16-inch/50-caliber Mark 7 gun")[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-8) in three triple-[gun turrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_turret "Gun turret") on the [centerline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centerline_(nautical) "Centerline (nautical)"), two of which were placed in a [superfiring pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfire "Superfire") forward of the [superstructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superstructure "Superstructure"), with the third aft. Going from [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") to [stern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stern "Stern"), the turrets were designated I, II, and III. Their [secondary battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_armament "Secondary armament") consisted of twenty [5 in (127 mm)/38 caliber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5%22/38_caliber_gun "5\"/38 caliber gun")[dual-purpose guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-purpose_gun "Dual-purpose gun") mounted in twin-gun turrets clustered [amidships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amidships "Amidships"), five turrets on each [broadside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadside_(naval) "Broadside (naval)"). Unlike their [sister ships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_ship "Sister ship")[_Iowa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Iowa_(BB-61) "USS Iowa (BB-61)") and _New Jersey_ that were the first pair of ships built, _Missouri_ and [_Wisconsin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Wisconsin_(BB-64) "USS Wisconsin (BB-64)") were completed with an [anti-aircraft suite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") of twenty quadruple mounts for [40 mm (1.6 in) Bofors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bofors_40_mm_L/60_gun "Bofors 40 mm L/60 gun")[AA guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AA_gun "AA gun"), nine mounts on each broadside and one each on the roofs of Turrets II and III. Forty-nine [20-millimeter (0.8 in) Oerlikon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon") light AA [auto-cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auto-cannon "Auto-cannon") in single mounts were distributed almost the length of the ships.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985323,_449-9)

The primary means of controlling the main armament are two Mark 38 [directors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_(military) "Director (military)") for the [Mark 38 fire-control system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_gun_fire-control_system "Ship gun fire-control system") mounted at the tops of the fore and aft fire-control towers in the superstructure. These directors were equipped with 25-foot-6-inch-long (7.8 m)[rangefinders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rangefinder "Rangefinder"), although their primary sensor was the [Mark 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_8_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 8 radar (page does not exist)")[fire-control radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-control_radar "Fire-control radar") mounted on their roofs. A secondary Mark 40 fire-control director was installed inside the armored [conning tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conning_tower "Conning tower") at the front of the superstructure that used the [Mark 27 fire-control radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_27_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 27 radar (page does not exist)") positioned on the top of the conning tower. Each turret is fitted with a rangefinder 46 feet (14 m) long and can act as a director for the other turrets. Four Mark 37 gunnery directors, two on the centerline at the ends of the superstructure and one on each broadside, control the five-inch guns. Each director was equipped with a 15-foot (4.6 m) rangefinder and a pair of radars on its roof. These were a [Mark 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_12_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 12 radar (page does not exist)") fire-control system and a [Mark 22](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_22_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 22 radar (page does not exist)")[height-finder radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Height-finder_radar "Height-finder radar"). Each 40 mm mount was remotely controlled by a Mark 51 director that incorporated a Mark 14 lead-computing [gyro gunsight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gyro_gunsight "Gyro gunsight") while the sailors that used the 20 mm gun used a Mark 14 sight to track their targets.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall91%E2%80%9394,_98%E2%80%93100,_102%E2%80%93103-10)

A [SK-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_radar "SK radar")[early-warning radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early-warning_radar "Early-warning radar") was fitted on the ship's [foremast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foremast "Foremast"); above it was a [SG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SG_radar "SG radar")[surface-search radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surface-search_radar "Surface-search radar"). The other SG radar was mounted at the top of the mainmast positioned on the rear [funnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funnel_(ship) "Funnel (ship)").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall109,_113-11)

The _Iowa_ s were built with two rotating [aircraft catapults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_catapult "Aircraft catapult") on their stern for [floatplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floatplane "Floatplane") and a large [crane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crane_(machine) "Crane (machine)") was fitted to recover them. Initially a trio of [Vought OS2U Kingfishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vought_OS2U_Kingfisher "Vought OS2U Kingfisher") were carried, but these were replaced by [Curtiss SC Seahawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtiss_SC_Seahawk "Curtiss SC Seahawk") in December 1944.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall94%E2%80%9395-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDraminski29-13)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell25-14)

### Protection

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Protection")]

The internal waterline [armor belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armor_belt "Armor belt") of the _Iowa_-class ships is 12.1 in (307 mm) thick and has a height of 10 ft 6 in (3.2 m). Below it is a [strake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strake "Strake") of Class B [homogeneous armor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolled_homogeneous_armor "Rolled homogeneous armor") plate that tapers in thickness from 12.1 inches at the top to 1.62 in (41 mm) at the bottom and is 28 ft (8.5 m) high. The two strakes of armor are inclined outwards at the top 19 degrees to improve the armor's resistance to horizontal fire. In general the vertical armor plates are made from Class A [cemented armor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krupp_armour#Krupp_cemented_armour "Krupp armour") and the horizontal armor from Class B or [special treatment steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_treatment_steel "Special treatment steel") (STS). The belt armor extends to the two transverse [bulkheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulkhead_(partition) "Bulkhead (partition)") fore and aft of the main-gun [barbettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbette "Barbette"), forming the [armored citadel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armored_citadel "Armored citadel"). Part of the lower armor belt extends aft from the rear bulkhead to protect the ships' steering gear. Its maximum thickness ranges from 13 to 13.5 in (330 to 343 mm) at the top and the plates taper to 5 inches at the bottom. Unlike the _Iowa_ and _New Jersey_, the armor plates in the forward transverse bulkhead in _Missouri_ and _Wisconsin_ have a maximum thickness of 14.5 in (368 mm) at the top that tapers to 11.7 in (297 mm). The aft bulkhead is a consistent 14.5 inches in thickness, but does not go below the lower belt extension due it meeting the armored third deck protecting the shafts and steering gears; the steering gear is closed by another 14.5-inch aft bulkhead.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall128%E2%80%93129,_170%E2%80%93171-15)

The main-gun turrets have Class B plates 19.5 in (495 mm) thick on their faces and 9.5 in (241 mm) of Class A plates on their sides. The armor plates protecting their barbettes range in thickness from 17.3 in (439 mm) to 14.8 in (376 mm) and 11.6 in (295 mm) with the thickest plates on the sides and the thinnest ones on the front and back. The sides of the conning tower are 17.3 in (440 mm) thick. The [main deck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_deck "Main deck") of the _Iowa_ s consists of 1.5 in (38 mm) of STS. Below this deck, the roof of the armored citadel is formed by 6 in (152 mm) of armor in two layers. Below this is a deck of 0.625-inch (16 mm) STS plates intended to stop splinters from shells that pierced the armored deck above it. The armor deck extends aft and the roof of the steering gear compartment is 6.2 in (160 mm) thick.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall129%E2%80%93130-16)

The [underwater protection system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_belt "Torpedo belt") of the _Iowa_-class battleships consists of three [watertight compartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertight_compartment "Watertight compartment") outboard of the lower armor belt and another behind it. The two outermost compartment are kept loaded with fuel oil or seawater to absorb the energy of the torpedo [warhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warhead "Warhead")'s detonation and slow the resulting splinters so they can be stopped by the lower armor belt. Behind the belt is a [holding bulkhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo_bulkhead "Torpedo bulkhead") intended to protect the ships' inner spaces from any splinters that might penetrate and the subsequent flooding. For protection against [naval mines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_mine "Naval mine"), the _Iowa_ s have a [double bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_bottom "Double bottom") that runs the full length of the ships and increases to a triple bottom except at the bow and stern.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall130,_132-17)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: History")]

### Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Missouri_ was the third ship of the United States Navy to be named after the [US state of Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) The ship was authorized by Congress in 1938[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell1-19) and ordered on 12 June 1940 with the [hull number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_number "Hull number") BB-63.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-NVR-20) The [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel") for _Missouri_ was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laid_down "Laid down") at the [Brooklyn Navy Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Navy_Yard "Brooklyn Navy Yard") on 6 January 1941 in [slipway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slipway "Slipway") 1. The ship was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 29 January 1944 before a crowd of 20,000 to 30,000 spectators. At the launching ceremony, the ship was [christened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_christening "Ship christening") by [Margaret Truman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Truman "Margaret Truman"), the [ship sponsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_sponsor "Ship sponsor") and daughter of [Harry S. Truman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman "Harry S. Truman"), then one of the senators from the ship's namesake state; Truman himself gave a speech at the ceremony. [Fitting-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitting-out "Fitting-out") work proceeded quickly, and the ship was [commissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning "Ship commissioning") on 11 June; [Captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(US_Navy) "Captain (US Navy)")[William Callaghan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_M._Callaghan "William M. Callaghan") served as her first commander.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell1%E2%80%9311-21)

_Missouri_ conducted her initial sea trials off New York, beginning on 10 July, and then steamed south to [Chesapeake Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay "Chesapeake Bay"), where she embarked on a [shakedown cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakedown_cruise "Shakedown cruise") and conducted training. During this period, she operated with the new large [cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruiser "Cruiser")[_Alaska_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Alaska_(CB-1) "USS Alaska (CB-1)"), which had also recently entered service, and several escorting [destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer"). The ship got underway on 11 November, bound for the [West Coast of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States"). She passed through the [Panama Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal "Panama Canal") a week later and continued on to [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"). There, additional fitting-out work was carried out at [Hunters Point Naval Shipyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunters_Point_Naval_Shipyard "Hunters Point Naval Shipyard") to prepare the vessel for use as a fleet [flagship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship "Flagship").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell14%E2%80%9325-22)

### World War II (1944–1945)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: World War II (1944–1945)")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_underway_in_August_1944.jpg/250px-USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_underway_in_August_1944.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Missouri_(BB-63)_underway_in_August_1944.jpg)

_Missouri_ underway in August 1944.

On 14 December, _Missouri_ departed San Francisco and sailed for [Ulithi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulithi "Ulithi") in the [Caroline Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Islands "Caroline Islands"), where she joined the rest of the fleet on 13 January 1945. She became a temporary [headquarters ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Headquarters_ship "Headquarters ship") for [Vice Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_admiral_(United_States) "Vice admiral (United States)")[Marc A. Mitscher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_A._Mitscher "Marc A. Mitscher").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) She then joined [Task Force 58](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Task_Force_58 "Task Force 58"), which [sortied](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortie "Sortie") on 27 January to launch an air attack on [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_Tokyo "Bombing of Tokyo") in support of the planned operation against [Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Iwo_Jima "Battle of Iwo Jima"). _Missouri_ served as part of the anti-aircraft screen for Task Group 58.2, centered on the carriers [_Lexington_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Lexington_(CV-16) "USS Lexington (CV-16)"), [_Hancock_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Hancock_(CV-19) "USS Hancock (CV-19)"), and [_San Jacinto_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_San_Jacinto_(CVL-30) "USS San Jacinto (CVL-30)"), during the raid on Tokyo.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer393-23) In addition to guarding the carriers, _Missouri_ and the other battleships acted as [oilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replenishment_oiler "Replenishment oiler") for the escorting destroyers, since the fleet's logistics train could not accompany the strike force during raids.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell27-24)

By 16 February, the task force had arrived off the coast of Japan to begin a series of [airstrikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airstrike "Airstrike"). The fleet then proceeded to Iwo Jima, which was invaded by American ground forces on 19 February. That evening, while patrolling with the carriers, _Missouri_ shot down a Japanese aircraft, probably a [Nakajima Ki-49](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nakajima_Ki-49 "Nakajima Ki-49") bomber. Task Force 58 departed in early March and returned to Ulithi to replenish fuel and ammunition. _Missouri_ was transferred to the [_Yorktown_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Yorktown_(CV-10) "USS Yorktown (CV-10)") task group, TG 58.4 at that time.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell28%E2%80%9330-25)

The ships departed again on 14 March for another round of air strikes on Japan.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer399-26) Four days later, _Missouri_'s anti-aircraft guns assisted in the destruction of four Japanese aircraft. American carrier aircraft struck a variety of targets around the [Inland Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seto_Inland_Sea "Seto Inland Sea"), which prompted a Japanese counter-attack that struck several carriers. The carrier [_Franklin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Franklin_(CV-13) "USS Franklin (CV-13)") was badly damaged and _Missouri_'s task group was detached to cover her withdrawal. By 22 March, _Franklin_ had left the area of operations and the group returned to the fleet to join the preparatory bombardment for the upcoming [invasion of Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Okinawa "Invasion of Okinawa").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)_Missouri_ was temporarily transferred to TF 59, along with her sisters _New Jersey_ and _Wisconsin_, to bombard the southern coast of [Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okinawa_Island "Okinawa Island") on 24 March,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer402-27) part of an effort to draw Japanese attention from the actual invasion target on the western side of the island, during which she fired 180 [rounds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartridge_(firearms) "Cartridge (firearms)"). _Missouri_ thereafter returned to TG 58.4.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer408-28)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/USS_Missouri_Zero_Kamikaze.jpg/250px-USS_Missouri_Zero_Kamikaze.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Missouri_Zero_Kamikaze.jpg)

A [kamikaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamikaze "Kamikaze") (top left) moments before striking _Missouri_'s side.

While operating with the carriers on 11 April, _Missouri_ came under attack from a [kamikaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamikaze "Kamikaze") that struck the side of the vessel below the main deck. The impact shattered the aircraft, throwing gasoline on the deck that rapidly ignited, but it was quickly suppressed by her crew. The attack caused superficial damage and the battleship remained on station. Two crewmen were wounded on 17 April when another kamikaze clipped the stern crane and crashed in the ship's [wake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_(physics) "Wake (physics)").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell33%E2%80%9337-29)_Missouri_ left Task Force 58 on 5 May to return to Ulithi; in the course of her operations off Okinawa, she claimed five aircraft shot down and another probable kill, along with partial credit for another six aircraft destroyed.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) While en route, _Missouri_ refueled from a fleet oiler that also brought the ship's new commander, Captain [Stuart S. Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuart_S._Murray "Stuart S. Murray"), who relieved Captain Callaghan on 14 May.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell37%E2%80%9338-30)

On 9 May, _Missouri_ reached Ulithi, before continuing on to [Apra Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apra_Harbor "Apra Harbor"), [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), where she arrived nine days later. [Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiral_(United_States) "Admiral (United States)")[William F. Halsey Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_F._Halsey_Jr. "William F. Halsey Jr."), the commander of [Third Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Third_Fleet "United States Third Fleet"), came aboard the ship that day, making her the fleet flagship of what was now re-designated as TF 38. On 21 May, the battleship got underway again, bound for Okinawa. She had reached the operational area by 27 May, when she took part in attacks on Japanese positions on the island. Together with the rest of the Third Fleet, she then steamed north to conduct a series of air strikes on Japanese airfields and other installations on the island of [Kyūshū](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ky%C5%ABsh%C5%AB "Kyūshū") on 2 and 3 June. The fleet was struck by [a major typhoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1945_Pacific_typhoon_season#Typhoon_Connie "1945 Pacific typhoon season") on the night of 5–6 June, which caused extensive damage to many ships of the fleet, though _Missouri_ suffered only minor damage. Another round of air strikes against targets on Kyūshū took place on 8 June. The fleet then withdrew to [Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyte_Gulf "Leyte Gulf") to replenish fuel and ammunition, arriving there on 13 June.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer418%E2%80%93419-31)

Third Fleet got underway again on 1 July to launch another series of attacks on the Japanese [Home Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_archipelago "Japanese archipelago"). During this period, _Missouri_ operated with TG 38.4. The carrier aircraft struck targets around Tokyo on 10 July, and then further north between [Honshū](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honsh%C5%AB "Honshū") and [Hokkaidō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hokkaid%C5%8D "Hokkaidō") from 13 to 14 July. The following day, _Missouri_ and several other vessels were detached to form TG 38.4.2 which was tasked with bombarding industrial facilities in [Muroran, Hokkaido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muroran,_Hokkaido "Muroran, Hokkaido"). A second bombardment mission followed on the night of 17–18 July, by which time the British battleship [HMS _King George V_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_King_George_V_(41) "HMS King George V (41)") had joined the formation.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer421%E2%80%93422-32) The battleships then returned to [screen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screening_(tactical) "Screening (tactical)") the carriers during strikes against targets around the Inland Sea and then Tokyo later in the month. After a brief pause, the carriers resumed attacks on northern Japan on 9 August, the same day as the [atomic bombing of Nagasaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_bombing_of_Nagasaki "Atomic bombing of Nagasaki"). The following day, rumors circulated that Japan would surrender, which was formally announced on the morning of 15 August.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

#### Signing of the Japanese Instrument of Surrender

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Signing of the Japanese Instrument of Surrender")]

Main article: [Japanese Instrument of Surrender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Instrument_of_Surrender "Japanese Instrument of Surrender")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/Douglas_MacArthur_signs_formal_surrender.jpg/250px-Douglas_MacArthur_signs_formal_surrender.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Douglas_MacArthur_signs_formal_surrender.jpg)

Allied sailors and officers watch [General of the Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_of_the_Army_(United_States) "General of the Army (United States)")[Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur "Douglas MacArthur") sign documents during the surrender ceremony aboard _Missouri_ on 2 September 1945. The unconditional surrender of the Japanese to the [Allies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II") officially ended the Second World War.

Over the course of the following two weeks, Allied forces made preparations to begin the [occupation of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_Japan "Occupation of Japan"). On 15 August Japan announced their surrender and on 21 August _Missouri_ sent a contingent of 200 officers and men to _Iowa_, which was to debark a landing party in Tokyo to begin the process of demilitarizing Japan. Two days later, Murray was informed that _Missouri_ would host the surrender ceremony, with the date scheduled for 31 August. The ship's crew immediately began preparations for the event, including cleaning and painting the vessel. _Missouri_ began the approach to [Tokyo Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Bay "Tokyo Bay") on 27 August, guided by the [_Hatsuzakura_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_destroyer_Hatsuzakura "Japanese destroyer Hatsuzakura"). That night, the ships stopped at [Kamakura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamakura "Kamakura"), where a courier brought the flag that [Commodore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodore_(United_States) "Commodore (United States)")[Matthew Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_C._Perry "Matthew C. Perry") had flown during his [expedition to open Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perry_Expedition "Perry Expedition") in 1853; the flag was to be displayed during the surrender ceremony. The flotilla then entered Tokyo Bay on 29 August, and _Missouri_ was anchored close to where Perry had anchored his own vessels some ninety-two years earlier. Poor weather delayed the ceremony until 2 September.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell50%E2%80%9351,_53%E2%80%9357-33)

[Fleet Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_admiral_(United_States) "Fleet admiral (United States)")[Chester Nimitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Nimitz "Chester Nimitz") boarded shortly after 08:00, and [General of the Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_of_the_Army_(United_States) "General of the Army (United States)")[Douglas MacArthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_MacArthur "Douglas MacArthur"), the Supreme Commander for the Allies, came on board at 08:43. The Japanese representatives, headed by [Foreign Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Minister "Foreign Minister")[Mamoru Shigemitsu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamoru_Shigemitsu "Mamoru Shigemitsu"), arrived at 08:56, 2 September 1945. At 09:02, General MacArthur stepped before a battery of [microphones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone "Microphone") and opened the 23-minute surrender ceremony to the waiting world by stating,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell65-34) "It is my earnest hope—indeed the hope of all mankind—that from this solemn occasion a better world shall emerge out of the blood and carnage of the past, a world founded upon faith and understanding, a world dedicated to the dignity of man and the fulfillment of his most cherished wish for freedom, tolerance, and justice."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-35)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-37)

By 09:30 the Japanese emissaries had departed. During the afternoon of 5 September, Halsey transferred his flag to the battleship [_South Dakota_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_South_Dakota_(BB-57) "USS South Dakota (BB-57)"), and early the next day _Missouri_ departed Tokyo Bay. As part of the ongoing [Operation Magic Carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Magic_Carpet "Operation Magic Carpet") she received homeward-bound passengers at Guam, then sailed unescorted for Hawaii. She arrived at Pearl Harbor on 20 September and flew Admiral Nimitz's flag on the afternoon of 28 September for a reception.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell78-38)

### Post-war (1946–1950)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Post-war (1946–1950)")]

The next day, _Missouri_ departed Pearl Harbor bound for the [East Coast of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States"). She reached New York City on 23 October and hoisted the flag of [Atlantic Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Fleet_Forces_Command "United States Fleet Forces Command") commander Admiral [Jonas Ingram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Ingram "Jonas Ingram"). Four days later, the battleship fired a [21-gun salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21-gun_salute "21-gun salute") (the first of 3 that day) as Truman—who had since become President of the United States—boarded for [Navy Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_Day "Navy Day") ceremonies.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell86-39)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29%2C_USS_Power_%28DD-839%29_and_TCG_Yavuz_%28B-70%29_off_Istanbul_on_5_April_1946.jpg/250px-USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29%2C_USS_Power_%28DD-839%29_and_TCG_Yavuz_%28B-70%29_off_Istanbul_on_5_April_1946.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Missouri_(BB-63),_USS_Power_(DD-839)_and_TCG_Yavuz_(B-70)_off_Istanbul_on_5_April_1946.jpg)

_Missouri_ (center) and [TCG _Yavuz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMS_Goeben "SMS Goeben") (right) in the Bosphorus, April 1946

After an overhaul in the [New York Naval Shipyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Naval_Shipyard "New York Naval Shipyard")[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell356-40) that included the replacement of the Mark 8 fire-control radars with [Mark 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_13_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 13 radar (page does not exist)") models,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall92-41) and a training cruise to [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba"), _Missouri_ returned to New York. During the afternoon of 21 March 1946, she received the remains of the [Turkish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") Ambassador to the United States, [Munir Ertegun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munir_Ertegun "Munir Ertegun"). She departed on 22 March for [Gibraltar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gibraltar "Gibraltar"), and on 5 April anchored in the [Bosphorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosphorus "Bosphorus") off [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"). She rendered full honors, including the firing of 19-gun salutes during the transfer of the remains of the late ambassador and again during the funeral ashore.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell100%E2%80%93102-42) The arrival of the ship was one of the causes of the [Turkish Straits crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_Straits_crisis "Turkish Straits crisis") between Turkey and the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-43)[_[new archival link needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Archiving\_a\_source "Help:Archiving a source")_]

_Missouri_ departed Istanbul on 9 April and entered [Phaleron Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phaleron_Bay "Phaleron Bay"), [Piraeus, Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piraeus,_Greece "Piraeus, Greece"), the following day for a welcome by Greek government officials and [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communist "Anti-communist") citizens. Greece had become the scene of a [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_Civil_War "Greek Civil War") between the [pro-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_Greece "Communist Party of Greece")-dominated left-wing [resistance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resistance_during_World_War_II "Resistance during World War II") organization [EAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Liberation_Front_(Greece) "National Liberation Front (Greece)")-[ELAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ELAS "ELAS") and the returning Greek government-in-exile. The United States saw this as an important test case for its new doctrine of [containment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Containment "Containment") of the Soviet Union. The Soviets were also pushing for concessions in the [Dodecanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodecanese "Dodecanese") to be included in the [peace treaty with Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Peace_with_Italy,_1947 "Treaty of Peace with Italy, 1947") and for access through the [Dardanelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dardanelles "Dardanelles") strait between the [Black Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea "Black Sea") and the Mediterranean. The voyage of _Missouri_ to the eastern Mediterranean symbolized America's strategic commitment to the region. News media proclaimed her a symbol of US interest in preserving Greece and Turkey's independence.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/Helicopter_lands_on_USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_gun_turret%2C_1948_Midshipmen%E2%80%99s_Practice_Cruise_%2837781879662%29.jpg/250px-Helicopter_lands_on_USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_gun_turret%2C_1948_Midshipmen%E2%80%99s_Practice_Cruise_%2837781879662%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Helicopter_lands_on_USS_Missouri_(BB-63)_gun_turret,_1948_Midshipmen%E2%80%99s_Practice_Cruise_(37781879662).jpg)

A helicopter lands on a _Missouri_ gun turret during the 1948 Midshipmen's practice cruise.

_Missouri_ departed Piraeus on 26 April, touching at [Algiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algiers "Algiers") and [Tangiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangiers "Tangiers") before arriving at Norfolk on 9 May. She departed for [Culebra Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culebra_Island "Culebra Island") on 12 May to join Admiral Mitscher's [8th Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Eighth_Fleet "United States Eighth Fleet") in the Navy's first large-scale postwar Atlantic training maneuvers. The battleship returned to New York City on 27 May, and spent the next year steaming Atlantic coastal waters north to the [Davis Strait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Strait "Davis Strait") and south to the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") on various training exercises.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) On 3 December, during a gunnery exercise in the North Atlantic, a [star shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_shell "Star shell") fired by the [light cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_cruiser "Light cruiser")[_Little Rock_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Little_Rock_(CL-92) "USS Little Rock (CL-92)") accidentally struck the battleship, killing one crewman and wounding three others.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell110-44)

_Missouri_ arrived at [Rio de Janeiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro") on 30 August 1947 for the [Inter-American Conference for the Maintenance of Hemisphere Peace and Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-American_Conference_for_the_Maintenance_of_Hemisphere_Peace_and_Security "Inter-American Conference for the Maintenance of Hemisphere Peace and Security"). President Truman boarded on 2 September to celebrate the signing of the [Rio Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Treaty "Rio Treaty"), which broadened the [Monroe Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_Doctrine "Monroe Doctrine") by stipulating that an attack on any one of the signatory American countries would be considered an attack on all.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

The Truman family boarded _Missouri_ on 7 September 1947 to return to the United States and disembarked at Norfolk on 19 September. Her overhaul in New York, which lasted from 23 September to 10 March 1948[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) included upgrading most of her radar suite. The SK-2 system was replaced by a [SR-3 radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SR-3_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "SR-3 radar (page does not exist)") and both SG fire-control radars were removed, an improved [SG-6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SG-6_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "SG-6 radar (page does not exist)") replaced the forward antenna and the aft SG was exchanged for a [SP height-finding radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SP_radar "SP radar"); [Mark 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_25_radar?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mark 25 radar (page does not exist)") fire-control radars replaced the combination Mark 12/22 installations on the roofs of the Mark 37 directors.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall101,_110%E2%80%93112-45) After the overhaul, the ship worked up at [Guantanamo Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base "Guantanamo Bay Naval Base"). The summer of 1948 was devoted to midshipman and reserve training cruises. Also in 1948, _Missouri_ became the first battleship to host a [helicopter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter "Helicopter") detachment, operating two Sikorsky [HO3S-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikorsky_H-5 "Sikorsky H-5") machines for utility and rescue work.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-46) The battleship departed Norfolk on 1 November 1948 for a second three-week [Arctic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic "Arctic") cold-weather training cruise to the Davis Strait. During the next two years, _Missouri_ participated in exercises from the [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") coast to the Caribbean, alternated with two midshipman summer training cruises. She was overhauled at Norfolk Naval Shipyard from 23 September 1949 to 17 January 1950.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell365-47)

Throughout the latter half of the 1940s, the various service branches of the United States had been reducing their inventories from their World War II levels. For the Navy, this resulted in several vessels of various types being decommissioned and either sold for scrap or placed in one of the various [United States Navy reserve fleets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_reserve_fleets "United States Navy reserve fleets") scattered along the coasts. As part of this contraction, three of the _Iowa_-class battleships had been de-activated and decommissioned but President Truman refused to allow _Missouri_ to be decommissioned. Against the advice of [Secretary of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense "United States Secretary of Defense")[Louis Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_A._Johnson "Louis A. Johnson"), Secretary of the Navy [John L. Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_L._Sullivan_(Navy) "John L. Sullivan (Navy)"), and Chief of Naval Operations [Louis E. Denfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_E._Denfeld "Louis E. Denfeld"), Truman ordered _Missouri_ to be maintained with the active fleet partly because of his fondness for the battleship and partly because the battleship had been christened by his daughter Margaret.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-48)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-49)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/USS_Missouri_February_1_1950_Final_Pull.jpg/250px-USS_Missouri_February_1_1950_Final_Pull.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Missouri_February_1_1950_Final_Pull.jpg)

Configuration for final successful pull

Captain William D. Brown assumed command of the battleship on 10 December while she was being overhauled.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell145%E2%80%93148-50) Then the only US battleship in commission, _Missouri_ was proceeding from [Hampton Roads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_Roads "Hampton Roads") on her first training exercise at sea since the overhaul, early on 17 January 1950 when she [ran aground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_grounding_incident "USS Missouri grounding incident")1.6 mi (2.6 km) from [Thimble Shoal Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thimble_Shoal_Light "Thimble Shoal Light"), near [Old Point Comfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Point_Comfort "Old Point Comfort"). She hit shoal water a distance of three ship-lengths from the main channel.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) The error resulted from a combination of many factors, including Brown's inexperience maneuvering such a large ship. The grounding occurred during a particularly high tide making the effort to free her even more difficult as did having an abandoned [anchor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor "Anchor") becoming embedded in her hull. After off-loading ammunition, fuel and food to lighten the battleship,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell153%E2%80%93157-51) she was refloated on 1 February with the aid of [tugboats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboats "Tugboats"), [pontoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontoon_(boat) "Pontoon (boat)"), [beach gear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach_gear_(ship_salvage) "Beach gear (ship salvage)") and a rising tide.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEButler114%E2%80%93128-52)

After the subsequent [Naval Board of Inquiry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Board_of_Inquiry "Naval Board of Inquiry"), Brown and three of his officers were [court-martialled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court-martial "Court-martial"). Brown was relieved of command and his subordinates were reprimanded. Captain [Harold Page Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Page_Smith "Harold Page Smith") assumed command on 7 February as the _Missouri_'s repairs were being completed. Having repaired morale aboard during his tenure as the ship was relegated to training duties in an effort to cut costs by Johnson, Page Smith was replaced by Captain Irving Duke on 19 April.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell160%E2%80%93164-53)

### Korean War (1950–1953)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_Missouri_(BB-63)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Korean War (1950–1953)")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/F4U-4B_VF-113_CV-47_1950.JPEG/250px-F4U-4B_VF-113_CV-47_1950.JPEG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_Missouri_at_the_Harbor_of_Inchon,_Republic_of_Korea._Landing_of_Inchon_is_the_largest_amphibious_landing_since_World_War_2..jpg)

A [Vought F4U Corsair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vought_F4U_Corsair "Vought F4U Corsair") overflies [Inchon Harbor, Republic of Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Inchon "Battle of Inchon") with _Missouri_ below the aircraft's tail.

In 1950, the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") started, prompting the United States to intervene on behalf of the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") (UN). President Truman ordered US forces stationed in Japan into South Korea. Truman also sent US-based troops, tanks, [fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_aircraft "Fighter aircraft") and [bomber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomber "Bomber") aircraft, and a strong naval force to Korea to support the Republic of Korea. As part of the naval mobilization _Missouri_ was transferred to the [Pacific Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Pacific_Fleet "United States Pacific Fleet") and dispatched from Norfolk on 19 August to support UN forces on the Korean peninsula.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) Due to the urgency of her mission Duke took the battleship directly through a [hurricane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane") off the coast of [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") on 20 August that blew her helicopters off the stern and damaged her enough that she required nearly a week's worth of repairs once she reached Pearl Harbor.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell166%E2%80%93168-54)

_Missouri_ arrived just west of [Kyūshū](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ky%C5%ABsh%C5%AB "Kyūshū") on 14 September, where she became the flagship of Rear Admiral [Allan Edward Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allan_Edward_Smith?action=edit&redlink=1 "Allan Edward Smith (page does not exist)"). The first American battleship to reach Korean waters, she bombarded [Samchok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samchok "Samchok") on 15 September in an attempt to divert troops and attention from the [Incheon landings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Incheon "Battle of Incheon").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) After a brief visit to [Sasebo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Fleet_Activities_Sasebo "U.S. Fleet Activities Sasebo"), Japan, to resupply, the ship arrived at [Incheon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incheon "Incheon") on 19 September, and began bombarding North Korean troops as they retreated north.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell171%E2%80%93172-55) On 10 October she became flagship of Rear Admiral [John M. Higgins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Higgins_(admiral) "John Higgins (admiral)"), commander of Cruiser Division 5. She arrived at Sasebo on 14 October, where she became flagship of Vice Admiral [A. D. Struble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Dewey_Struble "Arthur Dewey Struble"), Commander, [Seventh Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Seventh_Fleet "United States Seventh Fleet"). After screening the carrier [_Valley Forge_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Valley_Forge_(CV-45) "USS Valley Forge (CV-45)") along the east coast of [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea "Korea"), she conducted bombardment missions from 12 to 26 October in the [Chongjin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chongjin "Chongjin") and [Tanchon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanchon "Tanchon") areas on the west coast, and at [Wonsan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonsan "Wonsan") where she again screened carriers eastward of Wonsan.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) During this time, [comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedian "Comedian")[Bob Hope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Hope "Bob Hope") visited the battleship and gave three performances for the crew.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell178-56)

MacArthur's amphibious landings at Incheon had severed the [Korean People's Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_People's_Army "Korean People's Army") (KPA) supply lines; as a result, the KPA had begun a lengthy retreat from South Korea into North Korea. This retreat was closely monitored by the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") (PRC), out of fear that the UN offensive against Korea would create a US-backed enemy on China's border, and out of concern that the UN offensive in Korea could evolve into a UN war against China.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-Dogfights-57) In an effort to dissuade UN forces from completely overrunning North Korea, the People's Republic of China issued diplomatic warnings that they would use force to protect North Korea, but these warnings were not taken seriously for a number of reasons.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-58)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-59) This changed abruptly on 19 October 1950, when the first of an eventual total of 380,000 [People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army "People's Liberation Army") soldiers under the command of General [Peng Dehuai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peng_Dehuai "Peng Dehuai") crossed into North Korea, launching a full-scale [assault against advancing UN troops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Chosin_Reservoir "Battle of Chosin Reservoir"). The PRC offensive forced UN troops to retreat. The _Missouri_ provided gunfire support during the [Hungnam evacuation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungnam_evacuation "Hungnam evacuation") in December until the last UN troops, the American [3rd Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3rd_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "3rd Infantry Division (United States)"), departed on 24 December.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/Forecastle_of_USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_in_heavy_seas_c1951.jpg/250px-Forecastle_of_USS_Missouri_%28BB-63%29_in_heavy_seas_c1951.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Forecastle_of_USS_Missouri_(BB-63)_in_heavy_seas_c1951.jpg)

The [forecastle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forecastle "Forecastle") of _Missouri_ in heavy seas c. 1951

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/KoreanWarNavyGunfire.jpg/250px-KoreanWarNavyGunfire.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KoreanWarNavyGunfire.jpg)

_Missouri_ fires her guns against enemy positions during the Korean War.

In early 1951 _Missouri_ alternated carrier escort duty and shore bombardments off the east coast of Korea until 19 March.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) During a visit to [Yokosuka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Fleet_Activities_Yokosuka "U.S. Fleet Activities Yokosuka"), Japan, Captain George Wright relieved Duke as commanding officer on 2 March.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell185,_389-60) The battleship arrived at Yokosuka on 24 March and departed the port four days later for the United States,[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) having fired 2,895 sixteen-inch rounds and 8,043 five-inch shells during her deployment.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell187-61) Upon her arrival at Norfolk on 27 April the ship became the flagship of Rear Admiral [James L. Holloway, Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_L._Holloway,_Jr. "James L. Holloway, Jr."), commander, Cruiser Force, Atlantic Fleet.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) From May to August, she engaged in two [midshipman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midshipman "Midshipman") training cruises. _Missouri_ entered [Norfolk Naval Shipyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norfolk_Naval_Shipyard "Norfolk Naval Shipyard") 18 October for an overhaul which lasted until 30 January 1952.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) Captain [John Sylvester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sylvester_(admiral) "John Sylvester (admiral)") assumed command of the ship the same day her overhaul began.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell389-62)

_Missouri_ spent the next six months training out of Guantanamo Bay and Norfolk and made a port visit to New York in May where she participated in Navy Day celebrations, hosting nearly 11,000 visitors.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell198%E2%80%93202-63) She returned to Norfolk on 4 August and entered Norfolk Naval Shipyard to prepare for a second tour in the Korean combat zone.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) Captain Warner Edsall relieved Sylvester at the beginning of the overhaul.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell202-64) The battleship departed Hampton Roads on 11 September and arrived at Yokosuka on 17 October.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)

Vice Admiral [Joseph J. Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_J._Clark "Joseph J. Clark"), commander of the Seventh Fleet, brought his staff onboard on 19 October. Her primary mission was to provide naval gunfire support, codenamed "Cobra strikes", in the Chaho-Tanchon area, at Chongjin, in the Tanchon-Sonjin area, and at Chaho, Wonsan, [Hamhung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamhung "Hamhung"), and Hungnam from 25 October through 2 January 1953.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) One of the ship's helicopters crashed on 21 December while trying to assess the damage from a bombardment; all three men aboard were killed.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell206%E2%80%93207-65)_Missouri_ put into Incheon on 5 January and then sailed to Sasebo. General [Mark W. Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_W._Clark "Mark W. Clark"), Commander in Chief, UN Command, and Admiral Sir [Guy Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Russell "Guy Russell"), the British [Commander-in-Chief, Far East Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-Chief,_Far_East_Fleet "Commander-in-Chief, Far East Fleet"), visited the battleship on 23 January. In the following weeks, _Missouri_ resumed "Cobra" missions along the east coast of Korea.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18) As part of these, the ship would enter Wonsan Harbor to bombard targets there. North Korea artillery fruitlessly engaged her there on two occasions, 5 and 10 March, as their shells were fused to burst in the air. In retaliation for the latter incident, _Missouri_'s five-inch guns fired 998 shells at the North Korean positions.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell209%E2%80%93210-66) The last bombardment mission by _Missouri_ was against the Kojo area on 25 March; she had fired 2,895 sixteen-inch and 8,043 five-inch shells during the deployment. The following day, Edsall suffered a fatal [heart attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_attack "Heart attack") while [conning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conn_(nautical) "Conn (nautical)") her through the [anti-submarine nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-submarine_net "Anti-submarine net") defending Sasebo Harbor. Captain Robert Brodie assumed command on 4 April.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-BrodieCapt-67)_Missouri_ was relieved as the Seventh Fleet flagship on 6 April by _New Jersey_ and departed Yokosuka on 7 April.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-18)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell211%E2%80%93212-68)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/68/Civil_Defense_Shelter_Sign_%28MSA%29_%2823736048800%29.jpg/250px-Civil_Defense_Shelter_Sign_%28MSA%29_%2823736048800%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Civil_Defense_Shelter_Sign_(MSA)_(23736048800).jpg)

[Civil Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_civil_defense "United States civil defense") shelter sign held by [Missouri Governor John Dalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_M._Dalton "John M. Dalton") (right) in 1963 beside _Missouri_ painting in Tokyo Bay on 4 July 1945, by William A. Knox.

_Missouri_ arrived at Norfolk on 4 May; Rear Admiral E. T. Woolridge, commander, Battleships-Cruisers, Atlantic Fleet, hoisted his flag aboard her 10 days later. She departed on 8 June on a midshipman training cruise to Brazil, Cuba and Panama and returned to Norfolk on 4 August. Woolridge hauled down his flag in October as he transferred to another ship; Rear Admiral Clark Green, commander of Battleship Division 2 replaced him. The battleship was overhauled in Norfolk Naval Shipyard from 20 November to 2 April 1954 that included replacing her 16-inch guns[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell215%E2%80%93219-69) and exchanging her SP radar for a [SPS-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AN/SPS-8 "AN/SPS-8") system that required strengthening the mainmast to handle its weight.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESumrall112-70) The day before the end of the overhaul, Captain [Taylor Keith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Keith?action=edit&redlink=1 "Taylor Keith (page does not exist)") relieved Brodie in command of the ship. As the flagship of Rear Admiral [Ruthven Libby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruthven_Libby?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ruthven Libby (page does not exist)"), who had relieved Woolridge, _Missouri_ departed Norfolk on 7 June as the flagship of the midshipman training cruise to [Lisbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon "Lisbon"), Portugal, [Cherbourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherbourg-Octeville "Cherbourg-Octeville"), France, and Cuba.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStillwell219%E2%80%93221,_224%E2%80%93227,_389-71) During this voyage _Missouri_ was joined by the other three battleships of her class, the only time the four ships sailed together.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Missouri_(BB-63)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKaplan166-72) She returned to Norfolk on 3 August and departed on 23 August to be placed in reserve on the West Coast.
